FMA10014.name: thoracic vertebra 9
FMA10014.definition: The ninth thoracic vertebra counting from the top down. Note that members of this class are not necessarily homologous[ncit,modified].

FMA10037.name: thoracic vertebra 10
FMA10037.definition: The tenth thoracic vertebra counting from the top down. Note that members of this class are not necessarily homologous[ncit,modified].

FMA10059.name: thoracic vertebra 11
FMA10059.definition: The eleventh thoracic vertebra counting from the top down. Note that members of this class are not necessarily homologous[ncit,modified].

FMA10081.name: thoracic vertebra 12
FMA10081.definition: The twelfth thoracic vertebra counting from the top down. Note that members of this class are not necessarily homologous[ncit,modified].

FMA10419.name: pancreatic duct
FMA10419.definition: A duct that collects and carries secretions of the exocrine pancreas to the intestine.

FMA10427.name: body wall
FMA10427.definition: The external portion of an animal body derived from ectoderm and mesoderm layers that encloses the body cavity.

FMA10428.name: thoracic wall
FMA10428.definition: The thoracic wall (or chest wall) is the boundary of the thoracic cavity. The bony portion is known as the thoracic cage. However, the wall also includes muscle, skin, and fascia.

FMA10429.name: abdominal wall
FMA10429.definition: The tissues that surround the organs that are present within the abdominal cavity. The abdominal wall tissue is composed of layers of fat, parietal peritoneum, fascia, and muscles.

FMA10446.name: intervertebral disk
FMA10446.definition: A pad of fibrocartilage between the articular surfaces of two successive vertebral centra which has nucleus pulposus at its core.

FMA10455.name: intervertebral disk of thoracic vertebra
FMA10455.definition: An intervertebral disk that is part of a thoracic region of vertebral column. A thoracic intervertebral disk connects at least one thoracic vertebra, either to another thoracic vertebra, or at one point on the vertebral colummn, to a lumbar vertebra.

FMA10636.name: costo-cervical trunk
FMA10636.definition: The costocervical trunk arises from the upper and back part of the subclavian artery, behind the scalenus anterior on the right side, and medial to that muscle on the left side.

FMA10645.name: musculo-phrenic artery
FMA10645.definition: An artery with its origin in the lateral terminal branch of the internal thoracic artery, with distribution to the diaphragm and the intercostal muscles, and with anastomoses to the branches of the pericardiacophrenic and inferior phrenic.

FMA10646.name: superior epigastric artery
FMA10646.definition: An artery that arises from the internal thoracic arteryand anastomoses with the inferior epigastric artery at the umbilicus and supplies the anterior part of the abdominal wall and some of the diaphragm.

FMA10659.name: deep cervical artery
FMA10659.definition: The deep cervical artery (Profunda cervicalis) is an artery of the neck.

FMA10662.name: inferior thyroid artery
FMA10662.definition: One of the three branches of the thyroid axis that supplies the thyroid gland and branches to form the ascending cervical, esophageal, inferior laryngeal, muscular and tracheal arteries.

FMA10664.name: transverse cervical artery
FMA10664.definition: The transverse cervical artery (transverse artery of neck, transversa colli artery) is a branch of the thyrocervical trunk, running at a higher level than the suprascapular artery.

FMA10665.name: superficial cervical artery
FMA10665.definition: It ascends beneath the anterior margin of the trapezius, distributing branches to it, and to the neighboring muscles and lymph glands in the neck, and anastomosing with the superficial branch of the descending branch of the occipital artery.
synonyms: superficial branch of transverse cervical artery

FMA10951.name: inferior vena cava
FMA10951.definition: A vein that carries deoxygenated blood from the lower half of the body into the right atrium of the heart.

FMA11338.name: ileocecal junction
FMA11338.definition: A point along the course of the gastrointestinal tract where the small intestine (ileum) ends as it opens into the cecal portion of the large intestine; occurs usually within the iliac fossa, demarcated internally as the ileocecal orifice.

FMA11359.name: cavity of right atrium
FMA11359.definition: Luminal space of the right atrium of the heart.

FMA12224.name: respiratory tube
FMA12224.definition: A tube in the respiratory system. Examples: bronchus, bronchiole, trachea.

FMA12516.name: calcareous tooth
FMA12516.definition: Skeletal element within the mouth (or in some species, upper part of the digestive tract) that is composed of dentine and is used in procuring or masticating food.

FMA12519.name: vertebral bone 1
FMA12519.definition: The first vertebral bone in the vertebral column.

FMA12520.name: vertebral bone 2
FMA12520.definition: The second vertebral bone in the vertebral column.

FMA12521.name: mammalian cervical vertebra 3
FMA12521.definition: The third of the seven cervical vertebrae[ncit,modified].
synonyms: third cervical vertebra of axial skeleton

FMA12522.name: mammalian cervical vertebra 4
FMA12522.definition: The fourth of the seven cervical vertebrae[ncit,modified].

FMA12523.name: mammalian cervical vertebra 5
FMA12523.definition: The fifth of the seven cervical vertebrae[ncit,modified].

FMA12524.name: mammalian cervical vertebra 6
FMA12524.definition: The sixth of the seven cervical vertebrae[ncit,modified].

FMA12525.name: mammalian cervical vertebra 7
FMA12525.definition: Vertebra prominens is the proper name for the seventh cervical vertebra. The most distinctive characteristic of this vertebra is the existence of a long and prominent spinous process which is palpable from the skin surface, hence the name. This spinous process is thick, nearly horizontal in direction, not bifurcated, but terminating in a tubercle to which the lower end of the ligamentum nuchae is attached.

FMA12823.name: incisor tooth
FMA12823.definition: Incisors are the first kind of tooth in heterodont mammals. They are located in the premaxilla above and mandible below. [WP,unvetted].

FMA12845.name: subcostal vein
FMA12845.definition: A vein that runs along the bottom of the lowest rib. Each subcostal vein gives off a posterior (dorsal) branch which has a similar distribution to the posterior ramus of an intercostal artery. [WP,modified].

FMA12846.name: cardiac vein
FMA12846.definition: Vein of heart that drains the myocardium.

FMA13072.name: lumbar vertebra 1
FMA13072.definition: The first lumbar vertebra counting from the top down. Note that members of this class are not necessarily homologous[ncit,modified].

FMA13073.name: lumbar vertebra 2
FMA13073.definition: The second lumbar vertebra counting from the top down. Note that members of this class are not necessarily homologous[ncit,modified].

FMA13074.name: lumbar vertebra 3
FMA13074.definition: The third lumbar vertebra counting from the top down. Note that members of this class are not necessarily homologous[ncit,modified].

FMA13075.name: lumbar vertebra 4
FMA13075.definition: The fourth lumbar vertebra counting from the top down. Note that members of this class are not necessarily homologous[ncit,modified].

FMA13076.name: lumbar vertebra 5
FMA13076.definition: The fifth lumbar vertebra counting from the top down. Note that members of this class are not necessarily homologous[ncit,modified].

FMA13087.name: section of aorta
FMA13087.definition: Any portion of the aorta including the ascending and descending aorta, and aortic arch or a portion of the aortic orifice of the left ventricle.

FMA13109.name: pectoralis minor
FMA13109.definition: The Pectoralis minor is a thin, triangular muscle, situated at the upper part of the chest, beneath the Pectoralis major. [WP,unvetted].

FMA13279.name: left anterior segmental artery
synonyms: anterior bronchopulmonary segment of left pulmonary artery
anterior segmental artery of left lung
anterior segmental artery of left upper lobe

FMA13295.name: diaphragm
FMA13295.definition: A thin musculomebranous barrier that separates the abdominal and thoracic cavities. Often used for breathing control.

FMA13303.name: humerus
FMA13303.definition: Paired endochondral long bone that extends between the pectoral girdle and the skeletal parts of the forelimb. [PHENOSCAPE:mah].

FMA13321.name: clavicle bone
FMA13321.definition: A paired dermal or endochondral bone that is part of the pectoral girdle. The clavicle may be in contact with the interclavicle or coracoid and forms an attachment site for pectoral musculature. [PHENOSCAPE:ad].

FMA13322.name: right clavicle
FMA13322.definition: A clavicle that is in the right side of a entire appendicular skeleton.

FMA13323.name: left clavicle
FMA13323.definition: A clavicle that is in the left side of a entire appendicular skeleton.

FMA13324.name: cephalic vein
FMA13324.definition: A superficial vein of the upper limb that communicates with the basilic vein via the median cubital vein at the elbow and is located in the superficial fascia along the anterolateral surface of the biceps brachii muscle. Superiorly the cephalic vein passes between the deltoid and pectoralis major muscles and through the deltopectoral triangle, where it empties into the axillary vein.

FMA13335.name: abdominal external oblique muscle
FMA13335.definition: The lateral abdominal wall muscle that is the most superficial, immediately superficial to the internal oblique.

FMA13338.name: infrahyoid muscle
FMA13338.definition: The infrahyoid muscles are a group of four pairs of muscles in the anterior part of the neck. (The term infrahyoid refers to the region below to the hyoid bone in the neck. ) Collectively, they are referred to as the strap muscles, because the muscles are long and flat much like a strap.

FMA13341.name: sternohyoid muscle
FMA13341.definition: The sternohyoid muscle is a thin, narrow muscle attaching the hyoid bone to the sternum, one of the paired strap muscles of the infrahyoid muscles serving to depress the hyoid bone. It is innervated by the ansa cervicalis. The muscle arises from the posterior border of the medial end of the clavicle, the posterior sternoclavicular ligament, and the upper and posterior part of the manubrium sterni.

FMA13342.name: omohyoid muscle
FMA13342.definition: The omohyoid muscle is a muscle at the front of the neck that consists of two bellies separated by an intermediate tendon. It belongs to the group of infrahyoid muscles. [WP,unvetted].

FMA13343.name: sternothyroid muscle
FMA13343.definition: The Sternothyreoideus (or Sternothyroid muscle) is shorter and wider than the Sternohyoideus, beneath which it is situated. It arises from the posterior surface of the manubrium sterni, below the origin of the Sternohyoideus, and from the edge of the cartilage of the first rib, and sometimes that of the second rib, it is inserted into the oblique line on the lamina of the thyroid cartilage.

FMA13344.name: thyrohyoid muscle
FMA13344.definition: The thyrohyoid muscle is a small, quadrilateral muscle appearing like an upward continuation of the Sternothyreoideus. It belongs to the infrahyoid muscles group. It arises from the oblique line on the lamina of the thyroid cartilage, and is inserted into the lower border of the greater cornu of the hyoid bone. [WP,unvetted].

FMA13354.name: intercostal muscle
FMA13354.definition: The respiratory muscles that arise from the lower border of one rib and insert into the upper border of the adjoining rib.

FMA13362.name: right lobe of liver
FMA13362.definition: The right lobe is much larger than the left; the proportion between them being as six to one. It occupies the right hypochondrium, and is separated from the left lobe on its upper surface by the falciform ligament; on its under and posterior surfaces by the left sagittal fossa; and in front by the umbilical notch.

FMA13363.name: left lobe of liver
FMA13363.definition: The left lobe is smaller and more flattened than the right. It is situated in the epigastric and left hypochondriac regions. Its upper surface is slightly convex and is moulded on to the diaphragm; its under surface presents the gastric impression and omental tuberosity. [WP,unvetted].

FMA13365.name: caudate lobe of liver
FMA13365.definition: The caudate lobe (posterior hepatic segment I, Spigelian lobe) is situated upon the postero-superior surface of the liver on the right lobe of the liver, opposite the tenth and eleventh thoracic vertebrae. It is bounded on the left side by the physiological division of the liver called the ligamentum venosum.

FMA13385.name: scalenus anterior
FMA13385.definition: The Scalenus anterior (Scalenus anticus), also known as anterior scalene muscle, lies deeply at the side of the neck, behind the Sternocleidomastoideus.

FMA13386.name: scalenus medius
FMA13386.definition: The Scalenus medius, the largest and longest of the three scalene muscles, arises from the posterior tubercles of the transverse processes of the lower six cervical vertebræ. It descendes along the side of the vertebral column to insert by a broad attachment into the upper surface of the first rib, between the tubercle and the subclavian groove. The brachial plexus and the subclavian artery pass anterior to it.

FMA13387.name: scalenus posterior
FMA13387.definition: The Scalenus posterior (Scalenus posticus), the smallest and most deeply seated of the three Scaleni, arises, by two or three separate tendons, from the posterior tubercles of the transverse processes of the lower two or three cervical vertebræ, and is inserted by a thin tendon into the outer surface of the second rib, behind the attachment of the serratus ventralis.

FMA13394.name: scapula
FMA13394.definition: Endochondral bone that is dorsoventrally compressed and provides attachment site for muscles of the pectoral appendage.

FMA13397.name: serratus ventralis
FMA13397.definition: The serratus ventralis is a muscle that originates on the surface of the upper eight or nine ribs at the side of the chest and inserts along the entire anterior length of the medial border of the scapula. [WP,unvetted].

FMA13401.name: serratus dorsalis superior muscle
FMA13401.definition: The serratus dorsalis superior is a thin, quadrilateral muscle, situated at the upper and back part of the thorax. It arises by a thin and broad aponeurosis from the lower part of the ligamentum nuchae, from the spinous processes of the seventh cervical and upper two or three thoracic vertebræ and from the supraspinal ligament.

FMA13402.name: serratus dorsalis inferior muscle
FMA13402.definition: A muscle that originates from the vertebrae and inserts in the ribs.

FMA13407.name: sternocleidomastoid
FMA13407.definition: A paired muscle in the superficial layers of the anterior portion of the neck. It acts to flex and rotate the head. It also acts as an accessory muscle of inspiration, along with the scalene muscles of the neck. [WP,unvetted].

FMA13410.name: subclavius
FMA13410.definition: The Subclavius is a small triangular muscle, placed between the clavicle and the first rib. Along with the pectoralis major and pectoralis minor muscles, the subclavius muscle makes up the anterior wall of the axilla.

FMA13413.name: subscapularis muscle
FMA13413.definition: The subscapularis is a large triangular muscle which fills the subscapular fossa and inserts into the lesser tubercle of the humerus and the front of the capsule of the shoulder-joint. [WP,unvetted].

FMA13478.name: vertebral column
FMA13478.definition: Subdivision of skeletal system that consists of all the vertebra and associated skeletal elements and joints in the body[modified from VSAO].

FMA13884.name: heart ventricle wall
synonyms: anatomical wall of lower chamber of heart
anatomical wall of ventricle of heart

FMA13889.name: pituitary gland
FMA13889.definition: The pituitary gland is an endocrine gland that secretes hormones that regulate many other glands [GO]. An endocrine gland located ventral to the diencephalon and derived from mixed neuroectodermal and non neuroectodermal origin [ZFIN].

FMA13894.name: intervertebral disk of lumbar vertebra
FMA13894.definition: An intervertebral disk that is part of a lumbar region of vertebral column. A lumbar intervertebral disk connects at least one lumbar vertebra, either to another thoracic vertebra, or at one point on the vertebral colummn, to a sacral vertebra.

FMA13895.name: intervertebral disk of cervical vertebra
FMA13895.definition: An intervertebral disk that is part of a cervical region of vertebral column. A cervical intervertebral disk connects at least one cervical vertebra, either to another cervical vertebra, or at one point on the vertebral colummn, to a thoracic vertebra.

FMA13896.name: intervertebral disk of third cervical vertebra
FMA13896.definition: An intervertebral disk that connects a mammalian cervical vertebra 3 and connects a mammalian cervical vertebra 4.

FMA13897.name: intervertebral disk of fourth cervical vertebra
FMA13897.definition: An intervertebral disk that connects a mammalian cervical vertebra 4 and connects a mammalian cervical vertebra 5.
synonyms: intervertebral disc of fourth cervical vertebra

FMA13898.name: intervertebral disk of fifth cervical vertebra
FMA13898.definition: An intervertebral disk that connects a mammalian cervical vertebra 5 and connects a mammalian cervical vertebra 6.
synonyms: intervertebral disc of fifth cervical vertebra

FMA13899.name: intervertebral disk of sixth cervical vertebra
FMA13899.definition: An intervertebral disk that connects a mammalian cervical vertebra 6 and connects a mammalian cervical vertebra 7.

FMA13900.name: intervertebral disk of seventh cervical vertebra
FMA13900.definition: An intervertebral disk that connects a thoracic vertebra and connects a mammalian cervical vertebra 7.

FMA14319.name: suprascapular vein
FMA14319.definition: The suprascapular vein is a vein running above the scapula. It empties into the external jugular vein.

FMA14331.name: splenic vein
FMA14331.definition: A vein arising from the splenic trabecular vein in the hilum of the spleen that drains into the portal vein.

FMA14332.name: superior mesenteric vein
FMA14332.definition: In anatomy, the superior mesenteric vein (SMV) is a blood vessel that drains blood from the small intestine. At its termination behind the neck of the pancreas, the SMV combines with the splenic vein to form the hepatic portal vein. The SMV lies to the right of the similarly named artery, the superior mesenteric artery, which originates from the abdominal aorta. [WP,unvetted].

FMA14333.name: common iliac vein
FMA14333.definition: A vein that drains the pelvis and lower limbs into the inferior vena cava.

FMA14334.name: renal vein
FMA14334.definition: Either of the pair of major vessels which arise from the renal hilus and return blood from the kidneys, suprarenal gland and the ureter to the inferior vena cava.

FMA14335.name: right renal vein
FMA14335.definition: A renal vein that drains the right kidney.

FMA14336.name: left renal vein
FMA14336.definition: A renal vein that drains the left kidney.

FMA14337.name: hepatic vein
FMA14337.definition: Vein that carries blood away from the liver[ZFA].

FMA14338.name: right hepatic vein
FMA14338.definition: A hepatic vein that is part of a right lobe of liver.

FMA14339.name: left hepatic vein
FMA14339.definition: A hepatic vein that is part of a left lobe of liver.

FMA14341.name: right testicular vein
FMA14341.definition: A vein that drains the left pampiniform plexus and empties into the left renal vein.

FMA14343.name: right suprarenal vein
FMA14343.definition: A vein that drains blood from the right adrenal gland into the inferior vena cava.

FMA14344.name: testicular vein
FMA14344.definition: A vein that carries deoxygenated blood from a single male gonad. It is the male equivalent of the ovarian vein, and is the venous counterpart of the testicular artery. It is a paired vein, with one supplying each testis.

FMA14345.name: left testicular vein
FMA14345.definition: A vein that drains the right pampiniform plexus and empties into the inferior vena cava.

FMA14348.name: suprarenal vein
FMA14348.definition: A vein that drains the adrenal gland.

FMA14349.name: left suprarenal vein
FMA14349.definition: A vein that drains blood from the left adrenal gland into the left renal artery.

FMA14539.name: cystic duct
FMA14539.definition: The tubular structure that conducts gall bladder contents from the gall bladder to the common bile duct.

FMA14541.name: caecum
FMA14541.definition: A pouch in the digestive tract that connects the ileum with the ascending colon of the large intestine. It is separated from the ileum by the ileocecal valve, and is the beginning of the large intestine. It is also separated from the colon by the cecocolic junction.

FMA14542.name: vermiform appendix
FMA14542.definition: A blind-ended tube connected to the cecum, from which it develops embryologically[WP].

FMA14544.name: rectum
FMA14544.definition: The terminal portion of the intestinal tube, terminating with the anus.

FMA14545.name: ascending colon
FMA14545.definition: Section of colon which is distal to the cecum and proximal to the transversecolon.[FMA,modified].

FMA14546.name: transverse colon
FMA14546.definition: The proximal-distal subdivision of colon that runs transversely across the upper part of the abdomen, from the right to the left colic flexure. Continuous with the descending colon[BTO,modified].

FMA14547.name: descending colon
FMA14547.definition: The portion of the colon between the left colic flexure and the sigmoid colon at the pelvic brim; the portion of the descending colon lying in the left iliac fossa is sometimes called the iliac colon.

FMA14627.name: anterior abdominal wall
FMA14627.definition: The abdominal wall represents the boundaries of the abdominal cavity. The abdominal wall is split into the posterior (back), lateral (sides) and anterior (front) walls. There is a common set of layers covering and forming all the walls: the deepest being the extraperitoneal fat, the parietal peritoneum, and a layer of fascia which has different names over where it covers (eg transversalis, psoas fascia).

FMA14643.name: mesentery of small intestine
FMA14643.definition: The peritoneum responsible for connecting the jejunum and ileum (parts of the small intestine) to the back wall of the abdomen. Between the two sheets of peritoneum are blood vessels, lymph vessels, and nerves. This allows these parts of the small intestine to move relatively freely within the abdominopelvic cavity.

FMA14665.name: biliary tree
FMA14665.definition: A complex network of conduits that begins with the canals of Hering (intralobar bile duct) and progressively merges into a system of interlobular, septal, and major ducts which then coalesce to form the extrahepatic bile ducts, which finally deliver bile to the intestine, and in some species to the gallbladder.

FMA14668.name: common hepatic duct
FMA14668.definition: Predominantly extrahepatic bile duct which is formed by the junction of the right and left hepatic ducts, which are predominantly intrahepatic, and, in turn, joins the cystic duct to form the common bile duct[GAID].

FMA14669.name: right hepatic duct
FMA14669.definition: The duct that drains bile from the right half of the liver and joins the left hepatic duct to form the common hepatic duct.

FMA14670.name: left hepatic duct
FMA14670.definition: The duct that drains bile from the left half of the liver and joins the right hepatic duct to form the common hepatic duct.

FMA14678.name: extrahepatic bile duct
FMA14678.definition: Passages external to the liver for the conveyance of bile. These include the common bile duct and the common hepatic duct.

FMA14703.name: visceral peritoneum
FMA14703.definition: The inner layer of peritoneum that is wrapped around organs located inside the intraperitoneal space.

FMA14734.name: inferior phrenic artery
FMA14734.definition: The inferior phrenic arteries are two small vessels, which supply the diaphragm but present much variety in their origin. They may arise separately from the front of the aorta, immediately above the celiac artery, or by a common trunk, which may spring either from the aorta or from the celiac artery.

FMA14735.name: lumbar artery
FMA14735.definition: The lumbar arteries are in series with the intercostals. They are usually four in number on either side, and arise from the back of the aorta, opposite the bodies of the upper four lumbar vertebrC&. A fifth pair, small in size, is occasionally present: they arise from the middle sacral artery.

FMA14749.name: superior mesenteric artery
FMA14749.definition: Mesenteric artery that supplies the whole length of the small intestine except the superior part of the duodenum. It also supplies the cecum and the ascending part of the colon and about half the transverse part of the colon. It arises from the anterior surface of the aorta below the celiac artery at the level of the first lumbar vertebra.

FMA14750.name: inferior mesenteric artery
FMA14750.definition: Mesenteric artery that supplies the large intestine from the left colic (or splenic) flexure to the upper part of the rectum, which includes the descending colon, the sigmoid colon, and part of the rectum. Proximally, its territory of distribution overlaps (forms a watershed) with the middle colic artery, and therefore the superior mesenteric artery.

FMA14751.name: renal artery
FMA14751.definition: One of two laterally paired arteries that supplies the kidneys. These are large arteries that branch from the dorsal aorta in primitive vertebrates.

FMA14752.name: right renal artery
FMA14752.definition: Renal artery that supplies the right kidney.

FMA14753.name: left renal artery
FMA14753.definition: Renal artery that supplies the left kidney.

FMA14754.name: middle suprarenal artery
FMA14754.definition: The middle suprarenal arteries (middle capsular arteries; suprarenal arteries) are two small vessels which arise, one from either side of the abdominal aorta, opposite the superior mesenteric artery. They pass laterally and slightly upward, over the crura of the diaphragm, to the suprarenal glands, where they anastomose with suprarenal branches of the inferior phrenic and renal arteries.

FMA14758.name: testicular artery
FMA14758.definition: One of a pair of arteries that is a branch of the abdominal aorta that supplies blood to a male gonad.

FMA14759.name: right testicular artery
FMA14759.definition: A testicular artery that supplies a right testicle.
synonyms: trunk of right testicular arterial tree

FMA14760.name: left testicular artery
FMA14760.definition: A testicular artery that supplies a left testicle.
synonyms: trunk of left testicular arterial tree

FMA14764.name: common iliac artery
FMA14764.definition: The common iliac arteries are two large arteries, about 4cm long in adults but more than a centimetre in diameter, that originate from the aortic bifurcation. The arteries run inferolaterally, along the medial border of the psoas muscles to the pelvic brim, where they bifurcate into the external iliac artery and internal iliac artery.

FMA14765.name: right common iliac artery
synonyms: trunk of right common iliac arterial tree

FMA14766.name: left common iliac artery
synonyms: trunk of left common iliac arterial tree

FMA14768.name: left gastric artery
FMA14768.definition: An artery that arises from the celiac artery and supplies the stomach.

FMA14769.name: hepatic artery
FMA14769.definition: An artery that supplies the liver.

FMA14771.name: common hepatic artery
FMA14771.definition: In anatomy, the common hepatic artery is a short blood vessel that supplies oxygenated blood to the liver, pylorus (a part of the stomach), duodenum (a part of the small intestine), pancreas, and gall bladder. It arises from the celiac artery and has the following branches: the hepatic artery proper, the gastroduodenal artery and the right gastric artery.

FMA14772.name: proper hepatic artery
FMA14772.definition: The hepatic artery proper (also proper hepatic artery), arises from the common hepatic artery and runs alongside the portal vein and the common bile duct to form the portal triad. The hepatic artery proper gives off a small supraduodenal artery to the duodenal bulb.

FMA14773.name: splenic artery
FMA14773.definition: An artery that supplies the spleen.

FMA14775.name: gastroduodenal artery
FMA14775.definition: A small blood vessel in the abdomen that supplies blood directly to the pylorus (distal part of the stomach) and proximal part of the duodenum, and indirectly to the pancreatic head (via the anterior and posterior superior pancreaticoduodenal arteries).

FMA14776.name: right gastric artery
FMA14776.definition: An artery that branches from the proper hepatic artery and supplies the right side of the lesser curvature of the stomach and adjacent anterior and posterior surfaces.

FMA14778.name: right hepatic artery
FMA14778.definition: A hepatic artery that is part of a right lobe of liver.
synonyms: right branch of hepatic artery proper
right part of hepatic artery proper

FMA14779.name: left hepatic artery
FMA14779.definition: A hepatic artery that is part of a left lobe of liver.
synonyms: left part of hepatic artery proper

FMA14781.name: right gastroepiploic artery
FMA14781.definition: Artery that runs from right to left along the greater curvature of the stomach, between the layers of the greater omentum, anastomosing with the left gastroepiploic branch of the splenic artery.

FMA14782.name: anterior superior pancreaticoduodenal artery
FMA14782.definition: An artery that branches from the gastroduodenal artery and supplies the first and second parts (superior and descending parts) of the duodenum and the head of the pancreas.

FMA14784.name: posterior superior pancreaticoduodenal artery
FMA14784.definition: An artery that branches from the gastroduodenal artery and supplies the first and second parts of the duodenum, distal common bile duct and head of the pancreas.

FMA14787.name: dorsal pancreatic artery
FMA14787.definition: An artery that branches from the splenic artery and supplies the head, uncinate process, neck, body and tail of the pancreas. It anastamoses with the superior pancreaticoduodenal artery.
synonyms: Dorsal pancreatic part of splenic artery

FMA14792.name: greater pancreatic artery
FMA14792.definition: An artery that branches from the splenic artery and supplies the left half of the body and tail of the pancreas.

FMA14793.name: caudal pancreatic artery
FMA14793.definition: An artery that branches from the splenic artery and supplies the tail of the pancreas.

FMA14796.name: left gastroepiploic artery
FMA14796.definition: Artery that runs from left to right along the greater curvature of the stomach, between the layers of the greater omentum, and anastomoses with the right gastroepiploic.

FMA14805.name: inferior pancreaticoduodenal artery
FMA14805.definition: The inferior pancreaticoduodenal artery is a branch of the superior mesenteric artery or from its first intestinal branch, opposite the upper border of the inferior part of the duodenum. It courses to the right between the head of the pancreas and duodenum, and then ascends to anastomose with the anterior and posterior superior pancreaticoduodenal artery.

FMA14809.name: ileal artery
FMA14809.definition: The ileal arteries feed oxygenated blood into the ileum, a portion of the small intestine in mammals, reptiles, and birds. They are branches of the superior mesenteric artery.
synonyms: ileal branch of superior mesenteric artery

FMA14810.name: middle colic artery
FMA14810.definition: The middle colic artery is a branch of the superior mesenteric artery that mostly supplies the transverse colon. It arises just below the pancreas, and, passing downward and forward between the layers of the transverse mesocolon, divides into two branches: right and left.

FMA14811.name: right colic artery
FMA14811.definition: The right colic artery may arise directly from the superior mesenteric artery (SMA) but often arises from a common trunk with the ileocolic artery or middle colic artery. It supplies the ascending colon.

FMA14815.name: ileocolic artery
FMA14815.definition: The Ileocolic Artery is the lowest branch arising from the concavity of the superior mesenteric artery. It passes downward and to the right behind the peritoneum toward the right iliac fossa, where it divides into a superior and an inferior branch; the inferior anastomoses with the end of the superior mesenteric artery, the superior with the right colic artery. Supplies the cecum, ileum, and appendix. [WP,unvetted].

FMA14816.name: anterior cecal artery
FMA14816.definition: An artery that branches from the ileocolic artery and supplies the anterior portion of the cecum.

FMA14817.name: posterior cecal artery
FMA14817.definition: An artery that branches from the ileocolic artery and supplies the posterior portion of the cecum.

FMA14818.name: appendicular artery
FMA14818.definition: An artery that commonly arises from the terminal branch of the ileocolic artery, or less commonly from the posterior cecal artery or an ileal artery. It descends behind the termination of the ileum and enters the mesoappendix of the vermiform appendix. It runs near the free margin of the mesoappendix and ends in branches which supply the appendix.

FMA14819.name: ileal branch of ileocolic artery
FMA14819.definition: An artery that branches from the ileocolic artery and supplies the distal most ileum, ileocecal junction, cecum and appendix.
synonyms: Ileal branch of inferior branch of ileocolic artery

FMA14824.name: marginal artery of Drummond
FMA14824.definition: An arterial arcade that connects the superior and inferior mesenteric arteries and supplies the colon.

FMA14826.name: left colic artery
FMA14826.definition: The first branch of the inferior mesenteric artery (IMA) is the left colic artery. The left colic artery supplies blood flow to the distal third of the transverse colon and the entirety of the descending colon. Once diverging from the IMA, the left colic artery runs anterior to the left ureter, left internal spermatic vessels (males), and psoas major before branching into its ascending and descending segments.

FMA14828.name: ascending branch of left colic artery
FMA14828.definition: An artery that branches from the left colic artery and supplies the superior portion of the descending colon, the left colic flexure, and the right one half to one third of the transverse colon.

FMA14829.name: descending branch of left colic artery
FMA14829.definition: An artery that branches from the left colic artery and supplies the inferior portion of the descending colon.

FMA14830.name: sigmoid artery
FMA14830.definition: The sigmoid arteries, two or three in number, run obliquely downward and to the left behind the peritoneum and in front of the Psoas major, ureter, and internal spermatic vessels. Their branches supply the lower part of the descending colon, the iliac colon, and the sigmoid or pelvic colon; anastomosing above with the left colic, and below with the superior hemorrhoidal artery.

FMA14832.name: superior rectal artery
FMA14832.definition: The superior rectal artery (superior hemorrhoidal artery) is an artery that descends into the pelvis to supply blood to the rectum.

FMA14971.name: muscle layer of large intestine
FMA14971.definition: A muscle layer that is part of a large intestine.

FMA15041.name: taenia coli
FMA15041.definition: The taeniae coli (also teniae coli) are three separate longitudinal ribbons of smooth muscle on the outside of the ascending, transverse, descending and sigmoid colons. They are visible, and can be seen just below the serosa or fibrosa. They are the Mesocolic, Free and Omental Coli. The teniae coli contracts length wise to produce the haustra, the bulges in the colon.
synonyms: longitudinal band of large intestine muscularis

FMA15390.name: left gastroepiploic vein
FMA15390.definition: A vein that is a tributary of the splenic vein and drains the anterior and posterior body of the stomach and greater omentum.

FMA15391.name: inferior mesenteric vein
FMA15391.definition: A blood vessel that drains blood from the large intestine that usually terminates when reaching the splenic vein, which goes on to form the portal vein with the superior mesenteric vein (SMV). Anatomical variations include the IMV draining into the confluence of the SMV and splenic vein and the IMV draining in the SMV.

FMA15393.name: superior rectal vein
FMA15393.definition: A vein that is a tributary of the inferior mesenteric vein and drains the upper two thirds of the rectum and upper anal canal.

FMA15394.name: left colic vein
FMA15394.definition: A portal vein that drains the descending colon. It is a tributary of the inferior mesenteric vein, and follows the path of its corresponding artery, the left colic artery.

FMA15397.name: right gastroepiploic vein
FMA15397.definition: A vein that is a tributary of the superior mesenteric vein and drains the greater omentum and distal body and antrum of the stomach.

FMA15398.name: pancreaticoduodenal vein
FMA15398.definition: A vein running parallel to the superior and inferior pancreatico-duodenal arteries that drains blood from the pancreas and duodenum into the superior mesenteric or portal veins.

FMA15399.name: left gastric vein
FMA15399.definition: The Left gastric vein (or coronary vein) carries blood low in Oxygen, tributaries derived from both surfaces of the stomach; it runs from right to left along the lesser curvature of the stomach, between the two layers of the lesser omentum, to the esophageal opening of the stomach, where it receives some esophageal veins.

FMA15400.name: right gastric vein
FMA15400.definition: The right gastric vein, also known as the pyloric vein, drains blood from the lesser curvature of the stomach into the hepatic portal vein. It is part of the portal circulation.

FMA15405.name: ileal vein
FMA15405.definition: The veins that drain blood from the ileum into the superior mesenteric vein.

FMA15406.name: middle colic vein
FMA15406.definition: The middle colic vein drains the transverse colon. It is a tributary of the superior mesenteric vein, and follows the path of its corresponding artery, the middle colic artery. [WP,unvetted].

FMA15407.name: right colic vein
FMA15407.definition: A portal vein that drains the ascending colon. It is a tributary of the superior mesenteric vein, and travels with its corresponding artery, the right colic artery.

FMA15408.name: ileocolic vein
FMA15408.definition: The ileocolic vein is a vein which drains the ileum, colon, and cecum. [WP,unvetted].

FMA15629.name: right adrenal gland
FMA15629.definition: An adrenal gland that is in the right side of the abdomen.

FMA15630.name: left adrenal gland
FMA15630.definition: An adrenal gland that is in the left side of the abdomen.

FMA15900.name: urinary bladder
FMA15900.definition: Distensible musculomembranous organ situated in the anterior part of the pelvic cavity in which urine collects before excretion[MP].

FMA16202.name: fused sacrum
FMA16202.definition: A collection of sacral vertebrae in the sacral region that are fused and part of the bony pelvis.

FMA16203.name: lumbar region of vertebral column
FMA16203.definition: Subdivision of vertebral column that corresponds to the lumbar subdivision of the body, containing the lumbar vertebrae.

FMA16580.name: bony pelvis
FMA16580.definition: A ring of bone formed by the sacrum and the first few coccygeal vertebrae as the roof, the pubis and ischia as the floor and the ilia and the acetabular part of the ischia as the walls.

FMA16581.name: pelvic girdle region
FMA16581.definition: The organism subdivision that includes the pelvic girdle skeleton and associated soft tissue. Note that this includes both the skeletal elements and associated tissues (integument, muscle, etc). Examples: There are only two instances in an organism, right and left pelvic girdle regions.

FMA16582.name: right pelvic girdle region
FMA16582.definition: A pelvic girdle region that is in the right side of a multicellular organism.

FMA16583.name: left pelvic girdle region
FMA16583.definition: A pelvic girdle region that is in the left side of a multicellular organism.

FMA16585.name: innominate bone
FMA16585.definition: A fused bone consisting of the ilium, ischium and pubis. Together with the sacrum and coccyx, it comprises the pelvis. [WP,modified].

FMA18060.name: psoas major muscle
FMA18060.definition: The psoas major is a long fusiform muscle placed on the side of the lumbar region of the vertebral column and brim of the lesser pelvis. It joins the iliacus muscle to form the iliopsoas. In less than 50 per cent of subjects the psoas major is accompanied by the psoas minor. [WP,unvetted].

FMA18247.name: glans penis
FMA18247.definition: The conic expansion of the corpus spongiosum that forms the head of the penis.

FMA18255.name: epididymis
FMA18255.definition: The elongated structure connected to the posterior surface of the testis that transports, stores, and matures spermatozoa between testis and vas deferens.

FMA18805.name: external iliac artery
FMA18805.definition: The external iliac artery is a large artery in the pelvic region that carries blood to the lower limb. The external iliac artery is a paired artery, meaning there is one on each side of the body: a right external iliac artery and left external iliac artery. The external iliac artery is accompanied by the external iliac vein, which is located posterior to the artery. [WP,unvetted].

FMA18808.name: internal iliac artery
FMA18808.definition: The internal iliac artery (formerly known as the hypogastric artery) is the main artery of the pelvis. [WP,unvetted].

FMA18883.name: external iliac vein
FMA18883.definition: A large vein that connects the femoral vein to the common iliac vein. Their origin is at the inferior margin of the inguinal ligaments and they terminate when they join the internal iliac veins (to form the common iliac veins). Both external iliac veins are accompanied along their course by external iliac arteries. [WP,modified].

FMA18884.name: internal iliac vein
FMA18884.definition: A vein that begins near the upper part of the greater sciatic foramen, passes upward behind and slightly medial to the hypogastric artery and, at the brim of the pelvis, joins with the external iliac to form the common iliac vein. [WP,unvetted].

FMA18902.name: iliolumbar vein
FMA18902.definition: The iliolumbar vein is the vena comitans of the iliolumbar artery. The obturator nerve crosses superficial to it. A single vein is found more commonly than a double vein. It drains vertebral segments four and five. It is closely related to the ascending lumbar vein. [WP,unvetted].

FMA18905.name: lateral sacral vein
FMA18905.definition: A vein that is tributary of the internal iliac vein and drains the anterior surface of the sacrum.

FMA18914.name: obturator vein
FMA18914.definition: The obturator vein begins in the upper portion of the adductor region of the thigh and enters the pelvis through the upper part of the obturator foramen, in the obturator canal. It runs backward and upward on the lateral wall of the pelvis below the obturator artery, and then passes between the ureter and the hypogastric artery, to end in the hypogastric vein.

FMA18917.name: internal pudendal vein
FMA18917.definition: Accompanying vein of internal pudendal artery.

FMA19082.name: piriformis muscle
FMA19082.definition: The piriformis is a muscle in the gluteal region that originates from the anterior (front) part of the sacrum, the part of the spine in the gluteal region, and from the superior margin of the greater sciatic notch (as well as the sacroiliac joint capsule and the sacrotuberous ligament). It exits the pelvis through the greater sciatic foramen to insert on the greater trochanter of the femur.

FMA19083.name: obturator muscle
FMA19083.definition: One of: obturator externus or obturator internus.

FMA19086.name: muscle of pelvis
FMA19086.definition: Muscle (organ) which is a part of the pelvis. Examples: levator ani,.

FMA19088.name: coccygeus muscle
FMA19088.definition: e. peripheral to the pelvic floor), situated behind the levator ani and in front of the sacrospinous ligament. It is a triangular plane of muscular and tendinous fibers, arising by its apex from the spine of the ischium and sacrospinous ligament, and inserted by its base into the margin of the coccyx and into the side of the lowest piece of the sacrum.

FMA19090.name: pubococcygeus muscle
FMA19090.definition: The pubococcygeus muscle or PC muscle is a hammock-like muscle, found in both sexes, that stretches from the pubic bone to the coccyx (tail bone) forming the floor of the pelvic cavity and supporting the pelvic organs. It is part of the levator ani group of muscles.

FMA19091.name: puborectalis muscle
FMA19091.definition: The fibers which form a sling for the rectum are named the Puborectalis or Sphincter recti. They arise from the lower part of the symphysis pubis, and from the superior fascia of the urogenital diaphragm. They meet with the corresponding fibers of the opposite side around the lower part of the rectum, and form for it a strong sling.

FMA19092.name: iliococcygeus muscle
FMA19092.definition: The Iliococcygeus arises from the ischial spine and from the posterior part of the tendinous arch of the obturator fascia, and is attached to the coccyx and anococcygeal raphC); it is usually thin, and may fail entirely, or be largely replaced by fibrous tissue. It is part of the levator ani group of muscles. An accessory slip at its posterior part is sometimes named the Iliosacralis.

FMA19234.name: vas deferens
FMA19234.definition: A secretory duct that transports sperm from the testis. In mammals this is a continuation of the epididymis and ends in the prostatic urethra where it terminates to form ejaculatory duct.

FMA19386.name: seminal vesicle
FMA19386.definition: Either of a pair of glandular pouches that lie one on either side of the male reproductive tract posterolateral to the urinary bladder and in the human male secrete a sugar- and protein-containing fluid into the ejaculatory duct.

FMA19617.name: corpus spongiosum of penis
FMA19617.definition: Corpus spongiosum (also known as corpus cavernosum urethrae in older texts) is the mass of spongy tissue surrounding the male urethra within the penis.

FMA19618.name: corpus cavernosum penis
FMA19618.definition: One of the columns of erectile tissue forming the dorsum and sides of the penis.

FMA19667.name: urethra
FMA19667.definition: The fibromuscular tubular canal through which urine is discharged from the bladder to the exterior via the external urinary meatus; in males, the urethra is joined by the ejaculatory ducts and serves as a passageway for semen during ejaculation, as well as a canal for urine during voiding; in females, the urethra is shorter and emerges above the vaginal opening.

FMA19783.name: loose connective tissue
FMA19783.definition: Irregular connective tissue, the intercellular matrix of which contains a sparse irregular network of collagen and elastic fiber bundles. Examples: areolar tissue, neuroglial tissue, mucoid tissue.

FMA19795.name: dorsal artery of penis
FMA19795.definition: The Dorsal Artery of the Penis ascends between the crus penis and the pubic symphysis, and, piercing the inferior fascia of the urogenital diaphragm, passes between the two layers of the suspensory ligament of the penis, and runs forward on the dorsum of the penis to the glans, where it divides into two branches, which supply the glans and prepuce.

FMA20107.name: irregular connective tissue
FMA20107.definition: Connective tissue, which consists of a population of connective tissue cells, the intercellular matrix of which contains an irregular network of collagen and elastic fiber bundles. Examples: areolar tissue, mucoid tissue, connective tissue of peritoneum, connective tissue of fibrous pericardium.

FMA20111.name: mucoid tissue
FMA20111.definition: Loose connective tissue, the intercellular matrix of which consists predominantly of mucoid ground substance. Examples: Mucoid tissue of umbilical cord, mucoid tissue of vitreous body, mucoid tissue of nucleus pulposus.

FMA20218.name: mons pubis
FMA20218.definition: A structure composed of adipose tissue lying above the pubic bone of adult women, anterior to the symphysis pubis. The mons pubis forms the anterior portion of the vulva, and limits the perineal region proximally and anteriorly.

FMA20278.name: anterior abdominal wall muscle
FMA20278.definition: Any skeletal muscle organ that is part of a anterior abdominal wall. Examples: the obliques, pyramidalis and transversus abdominus.

FMA20289.name: lacrimal sac
FMA20289.definition: The upper dilated end of the nasolacrimal duct that is lodged in a deep groove formed by the lacrimal bone and frontal process of the maxilla; it connects the lacrimal canaliculi, which drain tears from the eye's surface, and the nasolacrimal duct, which conveys this fluid into the nasal cavity; like the nasolacrimal duct, the sac is lined by stratified columnar epithelium with mucus-secreting goblet cells, and is surrounded by connective tissue.

FMA20347.name: anal part of perineum
FMA20347.definition: The anal triangle is the posterior part of the perineum. It contains the anal canal. [WP,unvetted].

FMA20570.name: peritoneal mesentery
FMA20570.definition: Mesentery that is located in the peritoneum.

FMA20686.name: inferior epigastric artery
FMA20686.definition: The artery that arises from the external iliac artery and anastomoses with the superior epigastric artery.

FMA20734.name: superficial epigastric artery
FMA20734.definition: An artery that arises from the femoral artery and supplies the abdominal wall. It distributes branches to the superficial subinguinal lymph glands, the superficial fascia, and the integument; it anastomoses with branches of the inferior epigastric, and with its fellow of the opposite side.

FMA21162.name: inferior epigastric vein
FMA21162.definition: The blood vessel carrying deoxygenated blood that arises from the superior epigastric vein and empties into the external iliac vein.

FMA21185.name: femoral vein
FMA21185.definition: In the human body, the femoral vein is a blood vessel that accompanies the femoral artery in the femoral sheath. It begins at the adductor canal (also known as Hunter's canal) and is a continuation of the popliteal vein. It ends at the inferior margin of the inguinal ligament, where it becomes the external iliac vein. [WP,unvetted].

FMA21354.name: deep dorsal vein of penis
FMA21354.definition: The deep dorsal vein of the penis lies beneath the deep fascia of the penis; it receives the blood from the glans penis and corpora cavernosa penis and courses backward in the middle line between the dorsal arteries; near the root of the penis it passes between the two parts of the suspensory ligament and then through an aperture between the arcuate pubic ligament and the transverse ligament of the pelvis, and divides into two branches, which enter the pudendal plexus.

FMA21376.name: great saphenous vein
FMA21376.definition: The great saphenous vein (GSV), also greater saphenous vein, is the large (subcutaneous) superficial vein of the leg and thigh. The terms 'safaina' (Greek) and 'el safin' (Arabic) have both been claimed as the origin for the word 'saphenous'. [WP,unvetted].

FMA21384.name: superficial dorsal vein of penis
FMA21384.definition: A vein that drains the prepuce and skin of the penis, and, running backward in the subcutaneous tissue, inclines to the right or left, and opens into the corresponding superficial external pudendal vein, a tributary of the great saphenous vein..

FMA21496.name: ligament
FMA21496.definition: Dense regular connective tissue connecting two or more adjacent skeletal elements or supporting an organ.

FMA21930.name: external anal sphincter
FMA21930.definition: The Sphincter ani externus (external anal sphincter) is a flat plane of muscular fibers, elliptical in shape and intimately adherent to the integument surrounding the margin of the anus. [WP,unvetted].

FMA222905.name: proximal-distal subdivision of colon
FMA222905.definition: A section dividing a colon along a proximal-distal axis.

FMA22298.name: obturator internus
FMA22298.definition: The obturator internus muscle originates on the medial surface of the obturator membrane, the ischium near the membrane, and the rim of the pubis. It exits the pelvic cavity through the lesser sciatic foramen. The obturator internus is situated partly within the lesser pelvis, and partly at the back of the hip-joint.

FMA22299.name: obturator externus
FMA22299.definition: An adductor muscle that attaches to the femur and the pelvis. In humans, the obturator externus muscle is a flat, triangular muscle, which covers the outer surface of the anterior wall of the pelvis. It is sometimes considered part of the medial compartment of thigh, and sometimes considered part of the gluteal region. [WP,generalized].

FMA22310.name: iliacus muscle
FMA22310.definition: The iliacus is a flat, triangular muscle, which fills the iliac fossa. [WP,unvetted].

FMA22314.name: gluteus maximus
FMA22314.definition: The largest and most superficial of the three gluteal muscles [WP,unvetted].

FMA22315.name: gluteus medius
FMA22315.definition: One of three gluteal muscles, is a broad, thick, radiating muscle, situated on the outer surface of the pelvis. Its posterior third is covered by the gluteus maximus, its anterior two-thirds by the gluteal aponeurosis, which separates it from the superficial fascia and integument. [WP,unvetted].

FMA22317.name: gluteus minimus
FMA22317.definition: The smallest of the three gluteal muscles, situated immediately beneath the gluteus medius.

FMA22318.name: superior gemellus muscle
FMA22318.definition: The smaller of the two gemellus muscles that arises from the outer surface of the spine of the ischium, blends with the upper part of the tendon of the Obturator internus, and is inserted with it into the medial surface of the greater trochanter[WP].

FMA22319.name: gemellus muscle
FMA22319.definition: One of the two small muscular fasciculi, accessories to the tendon of the Obturator internus which is received into a groove between them.

FMA22320.name: inferior gemellus muscle
FMA22320.definition: Gemellus muscle that arises from the upper part of the tuberosity of the ischium, immediately below the groove for the Obturator internus tendon. It blends with the lower part of the tendon of the Obturator internus, and is inserted with it into the medial surface of the greater trochanter.

FMA22321.name: quadratus femoris
FMA22321.definition: The quadratus femoris is, as its name implies, a flat, quadrilateral skeletal muscle. Located on the posterior side of the hip joint, it is a strong lateral rotator and adductor of the thigh, but also acts to stabilize the femoral head in the Acetabulum.

FMA22353.name: sartorius muscle
FMA22353.definition: The Sartorius muscle - the longest muscle in the human body - is a long thin muscle that runs down the length of the thigh. Its upper portion forms the lateral border of the femoral triangle.

FMA22357.name: semitendinosus
FMA22357.definition: The semitendinosus is a muscle in the back of the thigh; it is one of the hamstrings. [WP,unvetted].

FMA22423.name: tensor fasciae latae muscle
FMA22423.definition: The tensor fasciae latae or tensor fasciæ latæ is a muscle of the thigh. [WP,unvetted].

FMA22427.name: muscle of posterior compartment of hindlimb stylopod
FMA22427.definition: Any of the posterior thigh muscles. [WP,modified].
synonyms: muscle of posterior compartment of thigh

FMA22430.name: rectus femoris
FMA22430.definition: The Rectus femoris muscle is one of the four quadriceps muscles of the human body. (The others are the vastus medialis, the vastus intermedius, and the vastus lateralis. All four combine to form the quadriceps tendon, which inserts into the patella and continues as the patellar ligament.

FMA22431.name: vastus lateralis
FMA22431.definition: The Vastus lateralis (Vastus externus) is the largest part of the Quadriceps femoris.

FMA22432.name: vastus medialis
FMA22432.definition: The vastus medialis, often called the 'teardrop' muscle, is a medially located muscle of the quadriceps. [WP,unvetted].

FMA22433.name: vastus intermedius
FMA22433.definition: The Vastus intermedius (Cruraeus) arises from the front and lateral surfaces of the body of the femur in its upper two-thirds, sitting under Rectus Femoris and from the lower part of the lateral intermuscular septum. Its fibers end in a superficial aponeurosis, which forms the deep part of the Quadriceps femoris tendon.

FMA22438.name: semimembranosus muscle
FMA22438.definition: The semimembranosus is a muscle in the back of the thigh. It is the most medial of the three hamstring muscles. [WP,unvetted].

FMA22440.name: pectineus muscle
FMA22440.definition: An adductor muscle that attaches to the pelvic bone and the femur. In humans, The pectineus muscle is a flat, quadrangular muscle, situated at the anterior part of the upper and medial aspect of the thigh. It can be classified in the medial compartment of thigh (when the function is emphasized) or the anterior compartment of thigh (when the nerve is emphasized). [WP,generalized].

FMA22441.name: adductor longus
FMA22441.definition: An adductor muscle that attaches to the hip and femur. In humans, it is a part of the adductor group of the thigh, that as the name suggests adducts the thigh. The adductor longus muscle forms the medial wall of the femoral triangle[WP, generalized].

FMA22442.name: adductor brevis
FMA22442.definition: The adductor brevis is a muscle in the thigh situated immediately behind the pectineus and adductor longus. It is somewhat triangular in form, and arises by a narrow origin from the outer surfaces of the superior and inferior rami of the pubis, between the gracilis and obturator externus. [WP].

FMA22443.name: adductor magnus
FMA22443.definition: An adductor muscle that attaches to the pelvic bone and the femur. In humans, the adductor magnus is a large triangular muscle, situated on the medial side of the thigh.

FMA22532.name: tibialis anterior
FMA22532.definition: A muscle that originates in the upper two-thirds of the lateral surface of the tibia and inserts into the medial cuneiform and first metatarsal bones of the foot. Its acts to invert the foot. It is situated on the lateral side of the tibia; it is thick and fleshy above, tendinous below. This muscle overlaps the anterior tibial vessels and deep peroneal nerve in the upper part of the leg. [WP,unvetted]. The M.

FMA22534.name: extensor digitorum longus
FMA22534.definition: A penniform muscle of the lateral front part of the hindlimb responsible for extension of the digits and dorsiflexion of the ankle.

FMA22538.name: fibularis tertius
FMA22538.definition: A muscle located in the lower limb that arises from the lower third of the anterior surface of the fibula; from the lower part of the interosseous membrane; and from an intermuscular septum between it and the peroneus brevis and inserted into the dorsal surface of the base of the metatarsal bone of the 5th digit. It is innervated by the deep fibular nerve.

FMA22539.name: fibularis longus
FMA22539.definition: A superficial muscle in the lateral compartment of the leg, and acts to evert and plantar flex the ankle. It is situated at the upper part of the lateral side of the leg, and is the most superficial of the three peroneus muscles. It is innervated by the superficial fibular nerve (superficial peroneal nerve). [WP,unvetted].

FMA22540.name: fibularis brevis
FMA22540.definition: The peroneus brevis muscle (or fibularis brevis) lies under cover of the peroneus longus, and is a shorter and smaller muscle.

FMA22542.name: soleus muscle
FMA22542.definition: A deep muscle of the triceps surae group, in the superficial posterior compartment of the leg.

FMA22543.name: plantaris
FMA22543.definition: Plantaris is a vestigial structure and one of the superficial muscles of the posterior crural compartment of the leg. It is innervated by the tibial nerve (S1, S2) . It is composed of a thin muscle belly and a long thin tendon. It is approximately 2-4 inches long, and is absent in 7 - 10% of the human population.

FMA22590.name: popliteus muscle
FMA22590.definition: The popliteus muscle in the leg is used to unlock the knee by laterally rotating the femur on the tibia during a closed chain movement (such as one with the foot in contact with the ground). [WP,unvetted].

FMA22593.name: flexor hallucis longus
FMA22593.definition: A deep muscle of the posterior compartment of the hindlimb that is innervated by the tibial nerve, arises from the fibula and insets in the distal phalanx of pedal digit 1.

FMA22594.name: muscle of vertebral column
FMA22594.definition: A muscle that is attached to a vertebra of the vertebral column.

FMA22653.name: splenius capitis
FMA22653.definition: A muscle that arises from the lower half of the ligamentum nuchæ, from the spinous process of the seventh cervical vertebra, and from the spinous processes of the upper three or four thoracic vertebræ and inserts the mastoid process of the temporal bone, and into the rough surface on the occipital bone just below the lateral third of the superior nuchal line[WP,modified].

FMA22654.name: axillary artery
synonyms: axillary part of trunk of subclavian artery

FMA22674.name: lateral thoracic artery
FMA22674.definition: A blood vessel that supplies oxygenated blood to the lateral structures of the thorax and breast. It originates from the axillary artery and follows the lower border of the Pectoralis minor muscle to the side of the chest, supplies the serratus ventralis muscle and the Pectoralis major muscle, and sends branches across the axilla to the axillary lymph nodes and Subscapularis muscle.

FMA22677.name: subscapular artery
FMA22677.definition: The subscapular artery, the largest branch of the axillary artery, arises at the lower border of the Subscapularis, which it follows to the inferior angle of the scapula, where it anastomoses with the lateral thoracic and intercostal arteries and with the descending branch of the transverse cervical, and ends in the neighboring muscles. About 4 cm.

FMA22680.name: anterior humeral circumflex artery
FMA22680.definition: An artery that branches from the axilliary artery and supplies the deltoid, biceps brachii, and coracobrachialis muscles, the glenohumeral joint, the proximal humeral head, and the skin overlying the anterior aspect of the proximal humerus. This artery courses laterally across the anterior surface of the humerus and anastomoses with the posterior humeral circumflex artery.

FMA22681.name: splenius cervicis
FMA22681.definition: A muscle that arises from the spinous processes of the third to the sixth thoracic vertebrae and inserts into the posterior tubercles of the transverse processes of the upper two or three cervical vertebrae[WP,modified].

FMA22684.name: posterior humeral circumflex artery
FMA22684.definition: An artery that branches from the axilliary artery and supplies the deltoid, teres major, teres minor, and long and lateral heads of the triceps brachii muscles, glenohumeral joint, and the cutaneous supply to the area posterolateral to the proximal humerus.

FMA22689.name: brachial artery
FMA22689.definition: The brachial artery is the major blood vessel of the (upper) arm. It is the continuation of the axillary artery beyond the lower margin of teres major muscle. It continues down the ventral surface of the arm until it reaches the cubital fossa at the elbow. It then divides into the radial and ulnar arteries which run down the forearm.
synonyms: brachial part of trunk of subclavian artery

FMA22695.name: deep brachial artery
FMA22695.definition: The arteria profunda brachii (also known as deep artery of the arm and the deep brachial artery) is a large vessel which arises from the medial and back part of the brachial, just below the lower border of the Teres major. [WP,unvetted].

FMA22702.name: iliocostalis lumborum
FMA22702.definition: The iliocostalis lumborum (iliocostalis muscle; sacrolumbalis muscle) is inserted, by six or seven flattened tendons, into the inferior borders of the angles of the lower six or seven ribs.

FMA22703.name: iliocostalis thoracis muscle
FMA22703.definition: The iliocostalis dorsi (musculus accessorius; iliocostalis thoracis) arises by flattened tendons from the upper borders of the angles of the lower six ribs medial to the tendons of insertion of the iliocostalis lumborum; these become muscular, and are inserted into the upper borders of the angles of the upper six ribs and into the back of the transverse process of the seventh cervical vertebra.

FMA22704.name: iliocostalis cervicis muscle
FMA22704.definition: The iliocostalis cervicis (cervicalis ascendens) arises from the angles of the third, fourth, fifth, and sixth ribs, and is inserted into the posterior tubercles of the transverse processes of the fourth, fifth, and sixth cervical vertebrae..

FMA22711.name: longissimus cervicis muscle
FMA22711.definition: A muscle with origin in transverse processes of upper thoracic vertebrae, and insertion in transverse processes of middle and upper cervical vertebrae that extends cervical vertebrae.

FMA22714.name: longissimus capitis
FMA22714.definition: A longissimus muscle that lies medial to the longissimus cervicis, between it and the semispinalis capitis. It arises by tendons from the transverse processes of the upper four or five thoracic vertebrae, and the articular processes of the lower three or four cervical vertebrae, and is inserted into the posterior margin of the mastoid process, beneath the splenius capitis and sternocleidomastoid.[WP,unvetted].

FMA22730.name: radial artery
FMA22730.definition: Branch of the brachial artery beginning below the elbow and extending down the forearm around the wrist and into the palm.

FMA22765.name: spinalis thoracis muscle
FMA22765.definition: Origin: spinous processes of two upper lumbar and two lower thoracic; insertion: spines of upper thoracic vertebrae; innervation: branches of spinal nerves; action: extends vertebral column.

FMA22796.name: ulnar artery
FMA22796.definition: The ulnar artery is the main blood vessel, with oxygenated blood, of the medial aspect of the forearm. It arises from the brachial artery and terminates in the superficial palmar arch, which joins with the superficial branch of the radial artery. It is palpable on the anterior and medial aspect of the wrist. Along its course, it is accompanied by a similarly named vein or veins, the ulnar vein or ulnar veins.

FMA22823.name: semispinalis muscle
FMA22823.definition: A transversospinalis muscle of the human body.

FMA22828.name: semispinalis thoracis
FMA22828.definition: The Semispinalis dorsi (or semispinalis thoracis) consists of thin, narrow, fleshy fasciculi, interposed between tendons of considerable length. It arises by a series of small tendons from the transverse processes of the sixth to the tenth thoracic vertebræ, and is inserted, by tendons, into the spinous processes of the upper four thoracic and lower two cervical vertebrae. [WP,unvetted].

FMA22829.name: semispinalis cervicis
FMA22829.definition: The semispinalis cervicis (semispinalis colli), thicker than the semispinalis dorsi, arises by a series of tendinous and fleshy fibers from the transverse processes of the upper five or six thoracic vertebræ, and is inserted into the cervical spinous processes, from the axis to the fifth inclusive. The fasciculus connected with the axis is the largest, and is chiefly muscular in structure. [WP,unvetted].

FMA22830.name: semispinalis capitis
FMA22830.definition: The Semispinalis capitis (Complexus) is situated at the upper and back part of the neck, deep to the Splenius, and medial to the Longissimus cervicis and capitis. It arises by a series of tendons from the tips of the transverse processes of the upper six or seven thoracic and the seventh cervical vertebræ, and from the articular processes of the three cervical above this.

FMA22834.name: superficial palmar arch
FMA22834.definition: The superficial palmar arch is formed predominantly by the ulnar artery, with a contribution from the superficial palmar branch of the radial artery. However, in some individuals the contribution from the radial artery might be absent, and instead anastomoses with either the princeps pollicis artery, the radialis indicis artery, or the median artery, the former two of which are branches from the radial artery.

FMA22908.name: basilic vein
FMA22908.definition: A superficial vein of the upper limb that drain parts of manus and forearm.

FMA22926.name: proper palmar digital vein
synonyms: tributary of common palmar digital vein

FMA22934.name: brachial vein
FMA22934.definition: A vein that accompanies the brachial artery between the shoulder and the elbow.

FMA22947.name: radial vein
FMA22947.definition: A vein that is tributary of the brachial vein and drains blood from the lateral structures of the forearm, carpal and metacarpal bones, joints of the hand, and lateral forearm muscles.

FMA22950.name: ulnar vein
FMA22950.definition: A vein that is tributary of the brachial vein and drains blood from the hand and medial and posterior aspect of forearm.

FMA22963.name: median basilic vein
FMA22963.definition: A vein between the biceps and pronator radii teres muscles that unites with the common ulnar vein to form the basilic vein within the forearm.

FMA23081.name: rotator muscle of the vertebral column
FMA23081.definition: Any of a number of short transversospinal muscles chiefly developed in cervical, lumbar, and thoracic regions, arising from the transverse process of one vertebra and inserted into the root of the spinous process of the next two or three vertebrae above, with nerve supply from the dorsal branches of the spinal nerve, and whose actions rotate the vertebral column.

FMA23113.name: subscapular vein
FMA23113.definition: A vein formed by the confluence of the thoracodorsal and circumflex scapular veins and accompanying the subscapular artery to drain into the axillary vein.

FMA231424.name: body proper
FMA231424.definition: The region of the organism associated with the visceral organs.

FMA23463.name: radius bone
FMA23463.definition: The major preaxial endochondral bone in the anterior zeugopod[Phenoscape].

FMA23466.name: ulna
FMA23466.definition: The major postaxial endochondral bone in the anterior zeugopod[Phenoscape].

FMA23709.name: radiale
FMA23709.definition: Endochondral proximal carpal bone articulating with the radius.

FMA23712.name: intermedium
FMA23712.definition: Endochondral carpal bone articulating with the ulnare and the radiale.

FMA23715.name: ulnare
FMA23715.definition: The postaxial bone of the proximal carpal region. Found in close approximation to the ulna, often in articulation[PHENOSCAPE:ad].

FMA23718.name: pisiform
FMA23718.definition: A laterally positioned sesamoid bone found in close proximity with and occasionally fused to the ulnare.

FMA23881.name: skeletal system
FMA23881.definition: Anatomical system that is a multi-element, multi-tissue anatomical cluster that consists of the skeleton and the articular system.

FMA23889.name: carpal bone
FMA23889.definition: A bone that is part of the carpal skeleton. Examples: scaphoid, lunate, capitate[cjm].

FMA23899.name: metacarpal bone of digit 1
FMA23899.definition: A metacarpal bone that distally_connected_to a proximal phalanx of manual digit 1.
synonyms: first digit of hand metacarpal bone

FMA23900.name: metacarpal bone of digit 2
FMA23900.definition: A metacarpal bone that distally_connected_to a proximal phalanx of manual digit 2.
synonyms: 2 nd digit of hand metacarpal bone

FMA23901.name: metacarpal bone of digit 3
synonyms: 3 rd digit of hand metacarpal bone

FMA23902.name: metacarpal bone of digit 4
FMA23902.definition: A metacarpal bone that distally_connected_to a proximal phalanx of manual digit 4.
synonyms: 4 th digit of hand metacarpal bone

FMA23903.name: metacarpal bone of digit 5
FMA23903.definition: A metacarpal bone that distally_connected_to a proximal phalanx of manual digit 5.
synonyms: 5 th digit of hand metacarpal bone

synonyms: proximal phalanx of first digit of hand
proximal phalanx of manual digit I

distal phalanx of manual digit I
