synonyms: distal phalanx of 5th digit of hand
distal phalanx of fifth digit of hand

FMA24138.name: cervical region of vertebral column
FMA24138.definition: That portion of the spine comprising the cervical vertebrae. The neck area of the spine.

FMA24189.name: dorsal part of neck
FMA24189.definition: The posterior region of the neck, including the suboccipital region.

FMA241998.name: cerebral hemisphere white matter
FMA241998.definition: White matter that is part of a cerebral hemisphere.
synonyms: white matter structure of cerebral hemisphere

FMA24217.name: dorsal thoracic segment of trunk
FMA24217.definition: Subdivision of thorax, which in humans is the posterior part of the thorax and is demarcated from the chest by the external surface of the posterolateral part of the rib cage and the anterior surface of the thoracic vertebral column; together with the chest, it constitutes the thorax.

FMA24228.name: sacral region
FMA24228.definition: A subdivision of an organism along the anterior-posterior axis in the pelvic region immediately posterior to the lumbar region and anterior to the caudal region. Sometimes an intermediate region is defined between the sacral and caudal.

FMA242675.name: ventricular system of central nervous system
FMA242675.definition: A set of structures containing cerebrospinal fluid in the brain. It is continuous with the central canal of the spinal cord[WP].

FMA242770.name: ventricle of nervous system
FMA242770.definition: A layer in the central nervous system that lines system of communicating cavities in the brain and spinal cord.

FMA24476.name: tibia
FMA24476.definition: The major preaxial endochondral bone in the posterior zeugopod[Phenoscape].

FMA24479.name: fibula
FMA24479.definition: The major postaxial endochondral bone in the posterior zeugopod[Phenoscape].

FMA24485.name: patella
FMA24485.definition: A large sesamoid bone found in the distal femur/proximal tibial region of the hindlimb of tetrapods. The patella is the attachment site for proximal hindlimb tendons.[PHENOSCAPE:ad].

FMA24491.name: tarsal bone
FMA24491.definition: A bone that is part of the tarsal skeleton. Examples: calcaneus, talus, centralia.

FMA24492.name: metatarsal bone
FMA24492.definition: The metatarsus or metatarsal bones are a group of five long bones in the pes located between the tarsal bones of the hind- and mid-pes and the phalanges of the toes. Lacking individual names, the metatarsal bones are numbered from the medial side (side of big toe): the first, second, third, fourth, and fifth metatarsal. The metatarsals are analogous to the metacarpal bones of the manus. [WP,unvetted].

FMA24496.name: calcaneus
FMA24496.definition: The postaxial bone of the proximal tarsals series[Phenoscape].

FMA24499.name: navicular bone of pes
FMA24499.definition: The oval-shaped tarsal bone found between the talus and the 3 cuneiform bones.

FMA24502.name: metatarsal bone of digit 1
FMA24502.definition: A metatarsal bone that distally_connected_to a proximal phalanx of pedal digit 1.

FMA24503.name: metatarsal bone of digit 2
FMA24503.definition: A metatarsal bone that distally_connected_to a proximal phalanx of pedal digit 2.

FMA24505.name: metatarsal bone of digit 4
FMA24505.definition: A metatarsal bone that distally_connected_to a proximal phalanx of pedal digit 4.

FMA24506.name: metatarsal bone of digit 5
FMA24506.definition: A metatarsal bone that distally_connected_to a proximal phalanx of pedal digit 5.

FMA24517.name: distal tarsal bone
FMA24517.definition: There are three cuneiform bones in the human foot: the medial cuneiform the intermediate cuneiform also known as the middle the lateral cuneiform. They are located between the navicular bone and the first, second and third metatarsal bones and are medial to the cuboid bone[WP, unvetted, human specific].

FMA24518.name: distal tarsal bone 1
FMA24518.definition: Endochondral tarsal bone articulating with centralia and metatarsal 1.

FMA24519.name: distal tarsal bone 2
FMA24519.definition: Endochondral tarsal bone articulating with centralia and metatarsal 2.

FMA24520.name: distal tarsal bone 3
FMA24520.definition: Endochondral tarsal bone articulating with centralia and metatarsal 3.

FMA24527.name: cuboid bone
FMA24527.definition: A tarsal bone that is formed from distal tarsals 4 and 5. [WP,modified].

FMA24728.name: face
FMA24728.definition: A subdivision of the head that has as parts the layers deep to the surface of the anterior surface, including the mouth, eyes, and nose (when present). In vertebrates, this includes the facial skeleton and structures superficial to the facial skeleton (cheeks, mouth, eyeballs, skin of face, etc).

FMA24816.name: anterior chest
FMA24816.definition: Subdivision of thorax which is anterior to the plane of the posterior boundary of the middle mediastinum.

FMA25058.name: intervertebral disk of axis
FMA25058.definition: An intervertebral disk that connects a vertebral bone 2 and connects a mammalian cervical vertebra 3.
synonyms: intervertebral disc of second cervical vertebra
intervertebral disk of second cervical vertebra

FMA25511.name: intervertebral joint
FMA25511.definition: The joint between adjacent vertebral bodies. May be composed of the nucleus pulposus, annular ligament, and the anterior and posterior longitudinal ligaments.

FMA256174.name: cerebral hemisphere white matter
FMA256174.definition: White matter that is part of a cerebral hemisphere.
synonyms: white matter structure of cerebral hemisphere

FMA256194.name: orbital gyrus
FMA256194.definition: The inferior or orbital surface of the frontal lobe is concave, and rests on the orbital plate of the frontal bone. It is divided into four orbital gyri by a well-marked H-shaped orbital sulcus. These are named, from their position, the medial, anterior, lateral, and posterior orbital gyri.

FMA25624.name: skeletal ligament
FMA25624.definition: Dense regular connective tissue connecting two or more adjacent skeletal elements[VSAO,modified].

FMA25625.name: nonskeletal ligament
FMA25625.definition: A ligament that does not connect two skeletal elements.

FMA256693.name: nucleus of thalamus
FMA256693.definition: A nucleus of brain that is part of a thalamus.

FMA258714.name: right dorsal thalamus
FMA258714.definition: A dorsal thalamus that is in_the_right_side_of a diencephalon.

FMA258716.name: left dorsal thalamus
FMA258716.definition: A dorsal thalamus that is in_the_left_side_of a diencephalon.

FMA259054.name: abdominal wall
FMA259054.definition: The tissues that surround the organs that are present within the abdominal cavity. The abdominal wall tissue is composed of layers of fat, parietal peritoneum, fascia, and muscles.

FMA259209.name: thoracic segment of trunk
FMA259209.definition: Subdivision of trunk that lies between the head and the abdomen.

FMA259211.name: abdominal segment of trunk
FMA259211.definition: The abdominal segment of the torso.

FMA265130.name: respiratory tract
FMA265130.definition: Anatomical structure that is part of the respiratory system. In mammals consists of upper and lower tracts.

FMA30320.name: duct
FMA30320.definition: A tubular structure that transports secreted or excreted substances.

FMA32514.name: prevertebral muscle
FMA32514.definition: One of the muscles deep to the prevertebral fascia on the anterior surface of the cervical and superior three thoracic vertebrae, symmetrically placed on each side of the median plane, including the longus colli, longus capitis, rectus capitis anterior, and rectus capitis lateralis muscles. innervated by anterior rami of cervical spinal nerves.

FMA32519.name: levator scapulae muscle
FMA32519.definition: An axial muscle that originates in the cervical vertebraae inserts on the scapula.

FMA32525.name: rectus capitis posterior major
FMA32525.definition: A muscle that arises by a pointed tendon from the spinous process of the axis and inserts into the lateral part of the inferior nuchal line of the occipital bone and the surface of the bone immediately below the line.

FMA32526.name: rectus capitis posterior minor
FMA32526.definition: A muscle that arise from the tubercle on the posterior arch of the and is inserted into the medial part of the inferior nuchal line of the occipital bone and the surface between it and the foramen magnum, and also takes some attachment to the spinal dura.

FMA32546.name: infraspinatus muscle
FMA32546.definition: The infraspinatus muscle is a thick triangular muscle, which occupies the chief part of the infraspinatous fossa. The infraspinatus is a muscle of the rotator cuff. [WP,unvetted].

FMA32549.name: teres major muscle
FMA32549.definition: Teres major is a muscle of the upper limb and one of six scapulohumeral muscles. It is a thick but somewhat flattened muscle. [WP,unvetted].

FMA32550.name: teres minor muscle
FMA32550.definition: A narrow, elongated muscle of the rotator cuff.

FMA32558.name: musculature
FMA32558.definition: A subdivision of the muscular system corresponding to a subdisivision of an organism.

FMA32672.definition: A sesamoid element that is composed of bone tissue.

FMA33302.definition: A carpal bone that proximally_connected_to a forelimb zeugopod skeleton.

FMA33303.name: distal carpal bone
FMA33303.definition: A distal carpal endochondral element that is composed primarily of a bone tissue.

FMA3734.name: aorta
FMA3734.definition: The main trunk of the systemic arterial system that carries blood from the heart to all the organs and other structures of the body, bringing oxygenated blood to all parts of the body in the systemic circulation.

FMA37347.name: muscle of pectoral girdle
FMA37347.definition: Any muscle organ that is part of a pectoral girdle region.

FMA37348.name: forelimb muscle
FMA37348.definition: Any muscle organ that is part of a forelimb.

FMA37349.name: pectoral muscle
FMA37349.definition: Muscles of the upper chest. The term may refer to one of two muscles, the pectoralis major and pectoralis minor. The former is a thick muscle in the anterior portion of the chest. Its action involves flexion, medial rotation, and adduction of the humerus. The latter is a thin muscle located beneath the pectoralis major. Its action involves lowering the scapula and raising the ribs.
synonyms: muscle of pectoral part of chest

FMA3736.name: ascending aorta
FMA3736.definition: The ascending aorta is the portion of the aorta in a two-pass circulatory system that lies between the heart and the arch of aorta[GO].

FMA37367.name: muscle of pelvic girdle
synonyms: muscle organ of pelvic girdle bone

FMA37373.name: abductor pollicis brevis muscle
FMA37373.definition: The abductor pollicis brevis is a muscle in the manus that functions as an abductor of the thumb.

FMA37378.name: flexor pollicis brevis muscle
FMA37378.definition: The flexor pollicis brevis is a muscle in the hand that flexes the thumb. It is one of three thenar muscles. It has both a superficial part and a deep part.

FMA37382.name: abductor digiti minimi of hand
FMA37382.definition: The Abductor minimi digiti (Abductor digiti quinti) is situated on the ulnar border of the palm of the hand.
synonyms: abductor digiti minimi muscle of hand

FMA37383.name: flexor digiti minimi brevis of hand
FMA37383.definition: The flexor digiti minimi brevis is a muscle in the hand that flexes the little finger. It lies in the same plane as the abductor digiti minimi, on its radial side.
synonyms: flexor digiti minimi brevis muscle of hand

FMA37384.name: opponens digiti minimi of hand
FMA37384.definition: The opponens minimi digiti (opponens digiti quinti in older texts) is a muscle in the hand. It is of a triangular form, and placed immediately beneath the palmaris brevis, abductor minimi digiti, and flexor brevis minimi digiti.
synonyms: opponens digiti minimi muscle of hand

FMA37448.name: abductor hallucis muscle
FMA37448.definition: The Abductor hallucis lies along the medial border of the pes and covers the origins of the plantar vessels and nerves. It arises from the medial process of the tuberosity of the calcaneus, from the laciniate ligament, from the plantar aponeurosis, and from the intermuscular septum between it and the Flexor digitorum brevis.

FMA37450.name: flexor digitorum brevis muscle
FMA37450.definition: The flexor digitorum brevis lies in the middle of the sole of the foot, immediately above the central part of the plantar aponeurosis, with which it is firmly united. Its deep surface is separated from the lateral plantar vessels and nerves by a thin layer of fascia.

FMA37453.name: lumbrical muscle of pes
FMA37453.definition: The lumbricals are four small skeletal muscles, accessory to the tendons of the flexor digitorum longus and numbered from the medial side of the pes; they arise from these tendons, as far back as their angles of division, each springing from two tendons, except the first.

FMA37456.name: interosseous muscle of pes
FMA37456.definition: Any of the interosseous muscles of the pes (foot). Includes the plantar and dorsal interossei.

FMA37458.name: plantar interosseous muscle of pes
FMA37458.definition: Any of three muscles with origin from the third, fourth, and fifth metatarsal bones, with insertion to the proximal phalanx of the same toes, with nerve supply from the lateral plantar nerve, and whose action adducts the three lateral toes.

FMA37664.name: coracobrachialis muscle
FMA37664.definition: The Coracobrachialis is the smallest of the three muscles that attach to the coracoid process of the scapula. (The other two muscles are pectoralis minor and biceps brachii. ) It is situated at the upper and medial part of the arm. It is perforated by and innervated by the musculocutaneous nerve. [WP,unvetted].

FMA37667.name: brachialis muscle
FMA37667.definition: The brachialis (brachialis anticus) is a muscle in the upper arm that flexes the elbow joint. It lies just deep of the biceps brachii, and is a synergist that assists the biceps brachii in flexing at the elbow. It makes up part of the floor of the region known as the cubital fossa. [WP,unvetted].

FMA3768.name: arch of aorta
FMA3768.definition: The convex portion of the aorta between the ascending and descending parts of the aorta; branches from it include the brachiocephalic trunk, the left common carotid artery, and the left subclavian artery; the brachiocephalic trunk further splits to form the right subclavian artery and the right common carotid artery.

FMA37682.name: short head of biceps brachii
FMA37682.definition: Proximally (towards the body), the short head of the biceps attaches to (originates from) the coracoid process at the top of the scapula.

FMA37683.name: long head of biceps brachii
FMA37683.definition: The long head originates on the supraglenoid tubercle just above the shoulder joint from where its tendon passes down along the intertubercular groove of the humerus into the joint capsule of the shoulder joint. When the humerus is in motion, the tendon of the long head is held firmly in place in the intertubercular groove by the greater and lesser tubercles and the overlying transverse humeral ligament.

FMA37704.name: anconeus muscle
FMA37704.definition: A small muscle on the posterior aspect of the elbow joint.

FMA3784.name: descending aorta
FMA3784.definition: The descending aorta is the portion of the aorta in a two-pass circulatory system from the arch of aorta to the point where it divides into the common iliac arteries[GO]. The descending aorta is part of the aorta, the largest artery in the body. The descending aorta is the part of the aorta beginning at the aortic arch that runs down through the chest and abdomen.

FMA3789.name: abdominal aorta
FMA3789.definition: Abdominal part of aorta: the distal part of the descending aorta, which is the continuation of the thoracic part and gives rise to the inferior phrenic, lumbar, median sacral, superior and inferior mesenteric, middle suprarenal, renal, and testicular or ovarian arteries, and celiac trunk[BTO]. The abdominal aorta is the largest artery in the abdominal cavity.

FMA3818.name: right marginal artery
FMA3818.definition: An artery that is a branch of the right coronary artery. It follows the acute margin of the heart supplying blood to the right ventricle.
synonyms: Marginal branch of right coronary artery

FMA38459.name: flexor carpi radialis muscle
FMA38459.definition: A muscle of the forearm that acts to flex and abduct the manus. [WP,unvetted].

FMA38462.name: palmaris longus muscle
FMA38462.definition: The palmaris longus is seen as a small tendon between the flexor carpi radialis and the flexor carpi ulnaris, although it is not always present. The muscle is absent in about 14 percent of the population, however this varies greatly with ethnicity. Absence of palmaris does not have any known effect on grip strength.

FMA38469.name: flexor digitorum superficialis
FMA38469.definition: An extrinsic flexor muscle of the fingers at the proximal interphalangeal joints.[WP].

FMA38478.name: flexor digitorum profundus
FMA38478.definition: A muscle in the forearm that flexes the manual digits[WP,modified].

FMA38481.name: flexor pollicis longus muscle
FMA38481.definition: A muscle in the forearm and hand that flexes the thumb. It lies in the same plane as the flexor digitorum profundus.

FMA38485.name: brachioradialis
FMA38485.definition: Brachioradialis is a muscle of the forearm that acts to flex the forearm at the elbow. It is also capable of both pronation and supination, depending on the position of the forearm. It is attached to the distal styloid process of the radius by way of the brachioradialis tendon, and to the lateral supracondylar ridge of the humerus.

FMA38494.name: extensor carpi radialis longus muscle
FMA38494.definition: Extensor carpi radialis longus is one of the five main muscles that control movements at the wrist. This muscle is quite long, starting on the lateral side of the humerus, and attaching to the base of the second metacarpal bone (metacarpal of the index finger). [WP,unvetted].

FMA38497.name: extensor carpi radialis brevis muscle
FMA38497.definition: The Extensor carpi radialis brevis is shorter and thicker than the extensor carpi radialis longus. The longus muscle can be found above the distal end of the Extensor carpi radialis brevis. [WP,unvetted].

FMA38500.name: extensor digitorum communis
FMA38500.definition: A muscle on the back of the forearm that extends the fingers and wrist.

FMA38503.name: extensor digiti minimi muscle
FMA38503.definition: The extensor minimi digiti (extensor digiti quinti proprius) is a slender muscle of the forearm, placed on the ulnar side of the Extensor digitorum communis, with which it is generally connected. It arises from the common Extensor tendon by a thin tendinous slip, from the intermuscular septa between it and the adjacent muscles.

FMA38506.name: extensor carpi ulnaris muscle
FMA38506.definition: Extensor carpi ulnaris is a muscle located in the forearm that acts to extend and adduct the wrist. Being an extensor muscle, extensor carpi ulnaris is on the posterior side of the forearm. [WP].

FMA38512.name: supinator muscle
FMA38512.definition: A muscle which originates on the distal humerus, inserts on the radius and accomplishes supination (rotation of the wrist).

FMA38515.name: abductor pollicis longus
FMA38515.definition: The Abductor pollicis longus lies immediately below the Supinator and is sometimes united with it. [WP,unvetted].

FMA38518.name: extensor pollicis brevis muscle
FMA38518.definition: The Extensor pollicis brevis lies on the medial side of, and is closely connected with, the Abductor pollicis longus.

FMA38521.name: extensor pollicis longus muscle
FMA38521.definition: The Extensor pollicis longus is much larger than the Extensor pollicis brevis muscle, the origin of which it partly covers.

FMA3862.name: left anterior descending artery
FMA3862.definition: An artery that branches from the left coronary artery and supplies the anterior wall of the left ventricle, the interventricular septum, and the apex of the heart.
synonyms: anterior interventricular branch of left coronary artery

FMA3895.name: circumflex branch of left coronary artery
FMA3895.definition: Branch of left coronary artery which runs perpendicular to the anterior interventricular branch of the left coronary artery on the left side of the interventricular sulcus and supplies the left side of the heart.
synonyms: left circumflex branch of left coronary artery

FMA3932.name: brachiocephalic artery
FMA3932.definition: The short first aortic arch branch and divides into the right subclavian artery and the right common carotid artery.

FMA3939.name: common carotid artery plus branches
FMA3939.definition: A bilaterally paired branched artery that originates from the aortic arches and divides into and includes as parts the internal and external carotid arteries[cjm].

FMA3941.name: right common carotid artery plus branches
FMA3941.definition: The rightmost of the two common carotid arteries, originating from in the neck from the brachiocephalic trunk.
synonyms: trunk of right common carotid tree

FMA3947.name: internal carotid artery
FMA3947.definition: A terminal branch of the left or right common carotid artery which supplies oxygenated blood to the brain and eyes[MP].

FMA3949.name: right internal carotid artery
FMA3949.definition: An internal carotid artery that branching_part_of a right common carotid artery plus branches.

FMA3951.name: subclavian artery
FMA3951.definition: One of two laterally paired arteries that supplies the pectoral appendages, usually branching from the dorsal aorta.

FMA3953.name: right subclavian artery
FMA3953.definition: The subclavian artery that supplies the right pectoral appendage.

FMA3956.name: vertebral artery
FMA3956.definition: The first branch of the left and right subclavian arteries that merge to form the single midline basilar artery; branches of the vertebral arteries supply the musculature of the neck.

FMA3960.name: internal thoracic artery
FMA3960.definition: An artery that supplies the anterior chest wall and the breasts. It is a paired artery, with one running along each side of the sternum, to continue after its bifurcation as the superior epigastric and musculophrenic arteries. [WP,unvetted].

FMA3990.name: thyrocervical trunk
FMA3990.definition: An artery that branches from the subclavian artery and supplies the thyroid gland, neck, and upper back regions.

FMA4058.name: left common carotid artery plus branches
FMA4058.definition: The leftmost of the two common carotid arteries, originating from the aortic arch in the thorax.
synonyms: trunk of left common carotid tree

FMA4062.name: left internal carotid artery
FMA4062.definition: An internal carotid artery that branching_part_of a left common carotid artery plus branches.

FMA4149.name: esophageal artery
FMA4149.definition: Any of several arteries that arise from the aorta and supply blood to the esophagus.

FMA42380.name: intrinsic muscle of manus
FMA42380.definition: Any of the intrinsic muscles of the manus (hand).

FMA43882.name: gracilis
FMA43882.definition: The most superficial muscle on the medial side of the thigh. It is thin and flattened, broad above, narrow and tapering below. It arises by a thin aponeurosis from the anterior margins of the lower half of the symphysis pubis and the upper half of the pubic arch.

FMA43894.name: anterior tibial artery
FMA43894.definition: The anterior tibial artery of the lower limb carries blood to the anterior compartment of the leg and dorsal surface of the foot, from the popliteal artery. It is accompanied by a deep vein, the anterior tibial vein, along its course. It crosses the anterior aspect of the ankle joint, at which point it becomes the dorsalis pedis artery. [WP,unvetted].

FMA43895.name: posterior tibial artery
FMA43895.definition: The posterior tibial artery of the lower limb carries blood to the posterior compartment of the leg and plantar surface of the foot, from the popliteal artery. It is accompanied by a deep vein, the posterior tibial vein, along its course. [WP,unvetted].

FMA43915.name: dorsalis pedis artery
FMA43915.definition: A blood vessel of the lower limb that carries oxygenated blood to the dorsal surface of the foot. It arises at the anterior aspect of the ankle joint and is a continuation of the anterior tibial artery. It terminates at the proximal part of the first intermetatarsal space, where it divides into two branches, the first dorsal metatarsal artery and the deep plantar artery.

FMA43925.name: medial plantar artery
FMA43925.definition: The medial plantar artery (internal plantar artery), much smaller than the lateral, passes forward along the medial side of the foot. It is at first situated above the Abductor hallucis, and then between it and the Flexor digitorum brevis, both of which it supplies.

FMA43956.name: plantar metatarsal artery
FMA43956.definition: The plantar metatarsal arteries (digital branches) are four in number, and run forward between the metatarsal bones and in contact with the Interossei. Each divides into a pair of plantar digital arteries which supply the adjacent sides of the toes. Near their points of division each sends upward an anterior perforating branch to join the corresponding dorsal metatarsal artery.
synonyms: plantar metatarsal branch of plantar arch

FMA44318.name: superficial epigastric vein
FMA44318.definition: The superficial epigastric vein is a vein which travels with the superficial epigastric artery. It joins the accessory saphenous vein near the fossa ovalis.

FMA44325.name: medial circumflex femoral vein
FMA44325.definition: A circumflex femoral vein that accompanies the medial circumflex femoral artery.

FMA44327.name: popliteal vein
FMA44327.definition: The popliteal vein course runs alongside the popliteal artery but carries the blood from the knee joint and muscles in the thigh and calf back to the heart. Its origin is defined by the junction of the posterior tibial vein and anterior tibial vein. It drains the peroneal vein before reaching the knee joint and turns into the femoral vein when leaving the adductor canal (also known as Hunter's canal).

FMA44331.name: anterior tibial vein
FMA44331.definition: A vein of the lower limb that carries blood from the anterior compartment of the leg to the popliteal vein which is forms when it joins with the posterior tibial vein. Like most deep veins, the anterior tibial vein is accompanied by an artery of the same name, the anterior tibial artery, along its course. [WP,unvetted].

FMA44332.name: posterior tibial vein
FMA44332.definition: A vein of the lower limb carries blood from the posterior compartment and plantar surface of the foot to the popliteal vein which it forms when it joins with the anterior tibial vein. Like most deep veins, the posterior tibial vein is accompanied by an artery of the same name, the posterior tibial artery, along its course. [WP,unvetted].

FMA44333.name: small saphenous vein
FMA44333.definition: The small saphenous vein (also lesser saphenous vein), is a relatively large vein of the superficial posterior leg. [WP,unvetted].

FMA44356.name: dorsal venous arch
FMA44356.definition: The dorsal venous arch of the foot is a superficial vein that connects the small saphenous vein and the great saphenous vein. Anatomically, it is defined by where the dorsal veins of the first and fifth digit, respectively, meet the great saphenous vein and small saphenous vein.

FMA44594.name: arcuate artery of foot
FMA44594.definition: The arcuate artery of the foot (metatarsal artery) arises a little anterior to the lateral tarsal artery; it passes lateralward, over the bases of the metatarsal bones, beneath the tendons of the Extensor digitorum brevis, its direction being influenced by its point of origin; and its anastomoses with the lateral tarsal and lateral plantar arteries.

FMA44660.name: dorsal digital artery of pes
FMA44660.definition: The dorsal digital arteries of foot are small arteries which supply the toes.

FMA45096.name: sesamoid bone of pes
FMA45096.definition: A sesamoid bone that is part of a pes.

FMA45621.name: pulmonary vascular system
FMA45621.definition: The part of the cardiovascular system consisting of all pulmonary arteries and all pulmonary veins.

FMA45623.name: systemic arterial system
FMA45623.definition: The part of the arterial system which carries oxygenated blood away from the heart to the body, and returns deoxygenated blood back to the heart.

FMA45626.name: systemic venous system
FMA45626.definition: The part of the venous system that drains the general body tissues[Kardong].

FMA45628.name: portal system
FMA45628.definition: In the circulatory system of animals, a portal venous system occurs when a capillary bed drains into another capillary bed through veins, without first going through the heart. Both capillary beds and the blood vessels that connect them are considered part of the portal venous system.

FMA45659.name: lower urinary tract
FMA45659.definition: Subdivision of urinary system which consists of the urinary bladder and the urethra.

FMA45662.name: lower respiratory tract
FMA45662.definition: The segment of the respiratory tract that starts proximally with the trachea and includes all distal structures including the lungs[WP,modified].

FMA45728.name: anatomical lobe
FMA45728.definition: A portion of an organ, such as the liver, lung, breast, or brain.

FMA45732.name: parenchyma
FMA45732.definition: Functional part of an organ in the body. This is in contrast to the stroma, which refers to the structural tissue of organs, being exactly, connective tissues.

FMA45738.name: platysma
FMA45738.definition: The platysma is a pharyngeal arch 2 muscle and a superficial facial muscle that participates in oral/pharyngeal behaviors and is innervated by the cervical branch of the facial nerve. It attaches to the mandible and it attaches to the skin of the head, neck, and thoracic region where it is found superficial to the clavicle. Burrows et al.

FMA45956.name: gastrocnemius medialis
FMA45956.definition: Missing definition for term UBERON:0011907. Please replace it using linked reference.

FMA45959.name: gastrocnemius lateralis
FMA45959.definition: Missing definition for term UBERON:0011908. Please replace it using linked reference.

FMA4613.name: subcostal artery
FMA4613.definition: An artery that runs along the bottom of the lowest rib. They constitute the lowest pair of branches derived from the thoracic aorta, and are in series with the intercostal arteries. Each passes along the lower border of the twelfth rib behind the kidney and in front of the Quadratus lumborum muscle, and is accompanied by the twelfth thoracic nerve.

FMA46290.name: suprahyoid muscle
FMA46290.definition: A muscle in the region above the hyoid bone in the neck. The suprahyoid muscles include digastric, stylohyoid, geniohyoid, and mylohyoid.

FMA46291.name: digastric muscle group
FMA46291.definition: A group of muscles (or in some classifications, muscle bellies) that are located under the jaw and attach to the base of the cranium and typically attaches to the hyoid apparatus via a common tendon.

FMA46308.name: longus capitis muscle
FMA46308.definition: A muscle that arises by four tendinous slips from the transverse processes of the third, fourth, fifth, and sixth cervical vertebrae and inserts into the inferior surface of the basilar part of the occipital bone.[WP,modified].

FMA46312.name: rectus capitis anterior
FMA46312.definition: A muscle situated immediately behind the upper part of the Longus capitis that arises from the anterior surface of the lateral mass of the atlas, and from the root of its transverse process that inserts into the inferior surface of the basilar part of the occipital bone immediately in front of the foramen magnum.

FMA46316.name: rectus capitis lateralis muscle
FMA46316.definition: A muscle that arises from the upper surface of the transverse process of the atlas and inserts into the under surface of the jugular process of the occipital bone.

FMA46320.name: mylohyoid muscle
FMA46320.definition: The mylohyoid is a pharyngeal arch I muscle that participates in oral/pharyngeal behaviors and is innervated by the nerve to mylohyoid and attaches to the midline raphe linking right and left mylohyoid and the mandible.

FMA46325.name: geniohyoid muscle
FMA46325.definition: The geniohyoid is a muscle that attaches to the mandible and the hyoid apparatus and is innervated by the first cervical nerve (C1).

FMA46472.name: nose
FMA46472.definition: The olfactory organ of vertebrates, consisting of nares, olfactory epithelia and the structures and skeletal framework of the nasal cavity.

FMA46562.name: muscle of larynx
FMA46562.definition: The muscles associated with the larynx.

FMA46565.name: skull
FMA46565.definition: Anatomical structure that is part of the head consisting entirely of cranium and mandible[WP].

FMA46576.name: posterior crico-arytenoid
FMA46576.definition: The posterior cricoarytenoid muscles are extremely small, paired muscles that extend from the posterior cricoid cartilage to the arytenoid cartilages in the larynx. By rotating the arytenoid cartilages laterally, these muscles abduct the vocal cords and thereby open the rima glottidis. Their action opposes the lateral cricoarytenoid muscles.

FMA46579.name: lateral crico-arytenoid
FMA46579.definition: The lateral cricoarytenoid (also anterior cricoarytenoid) muscles extend from the lateral cricoid cartilage to the ipsilateral arytenoid cartilage. By rotating the arytenoid cartilages medially, these muscles adduct the vocal cords and thereby close the rima glottidis, protecting the airway. (Their action is antagonistic to that of the posterior cricoarytenoid muscles.

FMA46582.name: transverse arytenoid
FMA46582.definition: The tranverse arytenoid crosses transversely between the two cartilages. It is an unpaired muscle running from one arytenoid to another to pull the arytenoids together.

FMA46583.name: oblique arytenoid
FMA46583.definition: The oblique arytenoid, the more superficial Arytenoid muscle, forms two fasciculi, which pass from the base of one cartilage to the apex of the opposite one, and therefore cross each other like the limbs of the letter X; a few fibers are continued around the lateral margin of the cartilage, and are prolonged into the aryepiglottic fold; they are sometimes described as a separate muscle, the Aryepiglotticus.

FMA46588.name: thyro-arytenoid
FMA46588.definition: The Thyroarytenoid is a broad, thin, muscle which lies parallel with and lateral to the vocal fold, and supports the wall of the ventricle and its appendix. It functions in fine tonal control of the vocal cords.

FMA46591.name: vocalis muscle
FMA46591.definition: The vocal muscle is the upper portion of the thyroarytenoid muscle which is primarily involved in producing speech.

FMA46602.name: aryepiglotticus muscle
FMA46602.definition: The aryepiglotticus is a muscle of the larynx running in the aryepiglottic fold from the arytenoid cartilage to the epiglottis.

FMA46619.name: chordate pharyngeal muscle
FMA46619.definition: A muscle that acts on the pharynx[WP, vetted].

FMA46620.name: constrictor muscle of pharynx
FMA46620.definition: Pharyngeal constrictor refers to one of the muscles that serves to constrict the pharynx. They include: Superior pharyngeal constrictor muscle Middle pharyngeal constrictor muscle Inferior pharyngeal constrictor muscle.

FMA46621.name: superior pharyngeal constrictor
FMA46621.definition: The superior pharyngeal constrictor muscle is a quadrilateral muscle, thinner and paler than the inferior pharyngeal constrictor muscle and middle pharyngeal constrictor muscle. [WP,unvetted].

FMA46622.name: middle pharyngeal constrictor
FMA46622.definition: The middle pharyngeal constrictor is a fanshaped muscle, smaller than the Inferior pharyngeal constrictor muscle.

FMA46623.name: inferior pharyngeal constrictor
FMA46623.definition: The inferior pharyngeal constrictor, the thickest of the three constrictors, arises from the sides of the cricoid and thyroid cartilage. Similarly to the superior and middle pharyngeal constrictor muscles, it is innervated by the vagus nerve (cranial nerve X), specifically, by branches from the pharyngeal plexus and by neuronal branches from the recurrent laryngeal nerve. [WP,unvetted].

FMA46664.name: stylopharyngeus muscle
FMA46664.definition: The stylopharyngeus is a muscle in the head that stretches between the styloid process and the pharynx.

FMA46665.name: salpingopharyngeus muscle
FMA46665.definition: The salpingopharyngeus muscle arises from the inferior part of the cartilage of the pharyngotympanic tube (Eustachian tube) in the nasal cavity; it passes downward and blends with the posterior fasciculus of the palatopharyngeus muscle. The salpingopharyngeus is known to raise the pharynx and larynx during deglutition (swallowing) and laterally draws the pharyngeal walls up.

FMA46666.name: palatopharyngeus muscle
FMA46666.definition: The palatopharyngeus or palatopharyngeal or pharyngopalatinus muscle is a long, fleshy fasciculus, narrower in the middle than at either end, forming, with the mucous membrane covering its surface, the palatopharyngeal arch.

FMA46689.name: tongue muscle
FMA46689.definition: The muscular portion of the tongue.

FMA46690.name: genioglossus muscle
FMA46690.definition: Either of a pair of lingual muscles with origin in the mandible, with insertion to the lingual fascia below the mucous membrane and epiglottis, with nerve supply from the hypoglossal nerve, and whose action depresses and protrudes the tongue.

FMA46691.name: hyoglossus muscle
FMA46691.definition: A muscle that attaches to the hyopid bone and to the tongue and is innervated by cranial nerve XII.

FMA46699.name: extrinsic muscle of tongue
FMA46699.definition: A muscle organ that attaches the tongue to some other structure.

FMA46726.name: palatal muscle
FMA46726.definition: The muscles of the palate are the glossopalatine, palatoglossus, levator palati(ni), musculus uvulae, palatopharyngeus, and tensor palati(ni).

FMA46727.name: levator veli palatini
FMA46727.definition: The levator veli palatini is the elevator muscle of the velum palatinum in the human body. During swallowing, it contracts, elevating the soft palate to help prevent food from entering the nasopharynx. It is innervated via the pharyngeal plexus, primarily by the vagus nerve (CN X). The levator veli palatini (Levator palati) is a thick, rounded muscle situated lateral to the choanC&.

FMA46730.name: tensor veli palatini
FMA46730.definition: The tensor veli palatini (tensor palati) is a broad, thin, ribbon-like muscle in the head that tenses the soft palate.

FMA46733.name: uvular muscle
FMA46733.definition: The musculus uvulae (azygos uvulae) is a muscle of the soft palate. It arises from the posterior nasal spine of the palatine bones and from the palatine aponeurosis. It descends to be inserted into the uvula and functions to move and shape it. It is innervated by the pharyngeal branch of the vagus nerve via the pharyngeal plexus[WP].

FMA46751.name: facial muscle
FMA46751.definition: A muscle innervated by a facial nerve.

FMA4694.name: left subclavian artery
FMA4694.definition: The subclavian artery that supplies the left pectoral appendage.

FMA4706.name: coronary sinus
FMA4706.definition: The short trunk that recieves most of the cardiac veins carrying the blood from the myocardium and delivers it to the right atrium, with the sinoatrial connection occurring between the inferior vena cava and the atrioventricular orifice.

FMA4707.name: great vein of heart
FMA4707.definition: The Great Cardiac Vein (left coronary vein) begins at the apex of the heart and ascends along the anterior longitudinal sulcus to the base of the ventricles. It then curves to the left in the coronary sulcus, and reaching the back of the heart, opens into the left extremity of the coronary sinus.

FMA4708.name: left marginal vein
FMA4708.definition: A vein that is a tributary of the great cardiac vein (left coronary vein) and drains blood from the left ventricle of the heart. It courses with the left marginal artery as it travels superiorly along the left cardiac border.

FMA4713.name: middle cardiac vein
FMA4713.definition: The middle cardiac vein commences at the apex of the heart, ascends in the posterior longitudinal sulcus, and ends in the coronary sinus near its right extremity.

FMA4714.name: small cardiac vein
FMA4714.definition: A vein running parallel to the right coronary artery in the coronary sulcus that drains into the right extremity of the coronary sinus.

FMA4720.name: anterior vena cava
FMA4720.definition: A vein that carries deoxygenated blood from the upper half of the body into the right atrium of the heart.

FMA4723.name: brachiocephalic vein
FMA4723.definition: The left and right brachiocephalic veins in the upper chest are formed by the union of each corresponding internal jugular vein and subclavian vein. This is at the level of the sternoclavicular joint. These great vessels merge to form the superior vena cava. The brachiocephalic veins are the major veins returning blood to the superior vena cava.

FMA4724.name: internal jugular vein
FMA4724.definition: One of two jugular veins that collect the blood from the brain, the superficial parts of the face, and the neck. [WP,unvetted].

FMA4725.name: subclavian vein
FMA4725.definition: The subclavian vein is a paired large vein, one on either side of the body. Their diameter is approximately that of the smallest finger.

FMA4729.name: internal thoracic vein
FMA4729.definition: A vessel that drains the chest wall and breats and arises from the superior epigastric vein, accompanies the internal thoracic artery along its course and terminates in the brachiocephalic vein.

FMA4731.name: superior epigastric vein
FMA4731.definition: A vein that drains into the internal thoracic vein, anastomosing with the inferior epigastric vein at the level of the umbilicus and drains the anterior part of the abdominal wall and some of the diaphragm. Along its course, it is accompanied by a similarly named artery, the superior epigastric artery.

FMA4732.name: musculo-phrenic vein
FMA4732.definition: Any of the veins that accompany the musculophrenic artery and drain blood from the upper abdominal wall, the lower intercostal spaces, and the diaphragm.

FMA4838.name: azygos vein
FMA4838.definition: An unpaired vein which in humans arises from the right ascending lumbar vein or the vena cava, enters the thorax through the aortic orifice in the diaphragm, and terminates in the superior vena cava; unlike humans, mice have a single and left-sided azygos vein that develops from the paired embryonic cardinal venous system and drains most of the right and left thoracic walls into the left anterior vena cava[MP].

FMA4844.name: right subcostal vein
FMA4844.definition: A vein that extends along the bottom of the twelfth rib on the right side of the body.

FMA49033.name: extra-ocular muscle
FMA49033.definition: Skeletal muscle derived from cranial mesoderm and controls eye movements.

FMA49035.name: superior rectus extraocular muscle
FMA49035.definition: The superior rectus muscle is a muscle in the orbit. It is one of the extraocular muscles. It is innervated by the superior division of the oculomotor nerve (Cranial Nerve III). In the primary position (looking straight ahead), the superior rectus muscle's primary function is elevation, although it also contributes to intorsion and adduction.

FMA49036.name: inferior rectus extraocular muscle
FMA49036.definition: A muscle in the orbit that depresses, adducts, and helps extort (rotate laterally) the eye. The inferior rectus muscle is the only muscle that is capable of depressing the pupil when it is in a fully abducted position.

FMA49037.name: medial rectus extraocular muscle
FMA49037.definition: The medial rectus muscle is a muscle in the orbit. As with most of the muscles of the orbit, it is innervated by the inferior division of the oculomotor nerve (Cranial Nerve III). This muscle shares an origin with several other extrinsic eye muscles, the anulus tendineus, or common tendon. It is the largest of the extraocular muscles and its only action is adduction of the eyeball. [WP,unvetted].

FMA49038.name: lateral rectus extra-ocular muscle
FMA49038.definition: The lateral rectus muscle is a muscle in the orbit. It is one of six extraocular muscles that control the movements of the eye (abduction in this case) and the only muscle innervated by the abducens nerve, cranial nerve VI. [WP,unvetted].

FMA49039.name: superior oblique extraocular muscle
FMA49039.definition: The superior oblique muscle, or obliquus oculi superior, is a fusiform muscle in the upper, medial side of the orbit whose primary action is downward, lateral rotation of the eye. One of the extraocular muscles, the superior oblique is the only muscle innervated by the trochlear nerve (the fourth cranial nerve).

FMA49040.name: inferior oblique extraocular muscle
FMA49040.definition: Thin, narrow muscle placed near the anterior margin of the floor of the orbit.

FMA49041.name: levator palpebrae superioris
FMA49041.definition: The levator palpebrae superioris (or levator muscle of upper eyelid) is the muscle in the orbit that elevates the superior (upper) eyelid. [WP,unvetted].

FMA49071.name: common tendinous ring
FMA49071.definition: A ring of fibrous tissue surrounding the optic nerve at its entrance at the apex of the orbit.

FMA49177.name: upper digestive tract
FMA49177.definition: The region of the digestive tract extending from the mouth cavity through pharynx esophagus stomach and duodenum.

FMA49179.name: lower digestive tract
FMA49179.definition: The region of the digestive tract extending from the beginning of the intestines to the anus[GO - gut definition].

FMA49184.name: mouth
FMA49184.definition: The proximal portion of the digestive tract, containing the oral cavity and bounded by the oral opening. In vertebrates, this extends to the pharynx and includes gums, lips, tongue and parts of the palate. Typically also includes the teeth, except where these occur elsewhere (e.g. pharyngeal jaws) or protrude from the mouth (tusks).

FMA49187.name: occipital region
FMA49187.definition: Anatomical cluster that is located in the posterior region of the cranium and forms the margin of the foramen magnum and occipital condyles.

FMA4944.name: hemiazygos vein
FMA4944.definition: The hemiazygos vein (vena azygos minor inferior) is a vein running superiorly in the lower thoracic region, just to the left side of the vertebral column.

FMA4951.name: left subcostal vein
FMA4951.definition: A vein that extends along the bottom of the twelfth rib on the left side of the body.

FMA49868.name: ophthalmic artery
FMA49868.definition: The ophthalmic artery is a branch of the internal carotid artery which supplies branches to supply the eye and other structures in the orbit. It enters the orbit together with the Optic nerve through the Optic foramen/canal. [WP,modified].

FMA49893.name: coronary artery
FMA49893.definition: An artery that supplies the myocardium.

FMA49911.name: right inferior pulmonary vein
FMA49911.definition: A pulmonary vein that drains blood from the inferior lobe of the right lung.

FMA49913.name: left inferior pulmonary vein
FMA49913.definition: A pulmonary vein that drains blood from the inferior lobe of the left lung.

FMA49914.name: right superior pulmonary vein
FMA49914.definition: A pulmonary vein that drains blood from the superior and middle lobes of the right lung.

FMA49916.name: left superior pulmonary vein
FMA49916.definition: A pulmonary vein that drains blood from the superior lobe and lingula of the left lung.

FMA50028.name: anterior cerebral artery
FMA50028.definition: One of a pair of arteries on the brain that supply oxygen to most medial portions of frontal lobes and superior medial parietal lobes. The 2 anterior cerebral arteries arise from the internal carotid artery and are part of the Circle of Willis.

FMA50031.name: branch of anterior cerebral artery
FMA50031.definition: An arterial branch arising from the anterior cerebral artery. It includes the callosomarginal artery, frontopolar artery, medial orbitofrontal artery, pericallosal artery, and recurrent artery of Heubner.

FMA50039.name: right coronary artery
FMA50039.definition: Coronary artery which runs along the right side of the heart and predominantly supplies the mycocardium of the right side of the heart[Wikipedia,modified].

FMA50040.name: left coronary artery
FMA50040.definition: Coronary artery which runs along the left side of the heart and predominantly supplies the mycocardium of the left side of the heart[Wikipedia,modified].

FMA50060.name: chest wall
FMA50060.definition: Subdivision of thorax which includes all structures from the skin to the costal pleura. Examples: There is only one chest wall.

FMA50084.name: posterior communicating artery
FMA50084.definition: One of a pair of right-sided and left-sided blood vessels in the circle of Willis. It connects the three cerebral arteries of the same side. Anteriorly, it is one portion of the terminal trifurcation of the internal carotid artery. The anterior cerebral artery and the middle cerebral artery are the other two branches of the trifurcation. Posteriorly, it communicates with the posterior cerebral artery.
synonyms: posterior communicating segment of the basilar artery

FMA50087.name: anterior choroidal artery
FMA50087.definition: The anterior choroidal artery originates from the internal carotid artery, though it also rarely arises from the middle cerebral artery.

FMA5011.name: accessory hemiazygos vein
FMA5011.definition: The accessory hemiazygos vein (vena azygos minor superior) is a vein on the left side of the vertebral column that generally drains the fifth through eighth intercostal spaces on the left side of the body[WP].

FMA50169.name: anterior communicating artery
FMA50169.definition: A blood vessel of the brain that connects the left and right anterior cerebral arteries. The anterior communicating artery connects the two anterior cerebral arteries across the commencement of the longitudinal fissure. Sometimes this vessel is wanting, the two arteries joining together to form a single trunk, which afterward divides; or it may be wholly, or partially, divided into two.

FMA5018.name: bone element
FMA5018.definition: Skeletal element that is composed of bone tissue.

FMA5022.name: muscle organ
FMA5022.definition: Organ consisting of a tissue made up of various elongated cells that are specialized to contract and thus to produce movement and mechanical work[GO].

FMA50382.name: anterior temporal artery
FMA50382.definition: A branch of the middle cerebral artery that supplies blood to the anterior part of the temporal lobe.

FMA50454.name: circle of Willis
FMA50454.definition: A circle of arteries that supply blood to the brain. The basilar artery and middle cerebral arteries, supplying the brain, are also considered part of the circle.

FMA50485.name: anterior parietal artery
FMA50485.definition: The artery that delivers blood to the anterior portion of the parietal lobe.

FMA50518.name: posterior inferior cerebellar artery
FMA50518.definition: The posterior inferior cerebellar artery (PICA), the largest branch of the vertebral, is one of the three main arterial blood supplies for the cerebellum.

FMA50531.name: anterior spinal artery
FMA50531.definition: A blood vessel that supplies the anterior portion of the spinal cord. It arises from branches of the vertebral arteries and is supplied by the anterior segmental medullary arteries, including the artery of Adamkiewicz, and courses along the anterior aspect of the spinal cord.

FMA50542.name: basilar artery
FMA50542.definition: A major artery that supplues the hindbrain and runs along the ventral keel of the hindbrain.

FMA50544.name: anterior inferior cerebellar artery
FMA50544.definition: A basilar artery branch that supplies the anterior portion of the inferior surface of the cerebellum.

FMA50573.name: superior cerebellar artery
FMA50573.definition: The superior cerebellar artery (SCA) arises near the termination of the basilar artery.

FMA50705.name: non-material anatomical boundary
FMA50705.definition: A non-material anatomical entity of two dimensions. Anatomical boundaries are contiguous structures.

FMA50720.name: artery
FMA50720.definition: An epithelial tube or tree of tibes that transports blood away from the heart[modified from AEO definition].

FMA50722.name: blood vessel
FMA50722.definition: A vessel through which blood circulates in the body.

FMA50723.name: vein
FMA50723.definition: Any of the tubular branching vessels that carry blood from the capillaries toward the heart.

FMA50735.name: hepatic portal vein
FMA50735.definition: A portal vein that transports nutrients from the digestive tract to the liver[Kardong].

FMA50737.name: celiac artery
FMA50737.definition: The first major branch of the abdominal aorta.

FMA50801.name: brain
FMA50801.definition: The brain is the center of the nervous system in all vertebrate, and most invertebrate, animals. Some primitive animals such as jellyfish and starfish have a decentralized nervous system without a brain, while sponges lack any nervous system at all. In vertebrates, the brain is located in the head, protected by the skull and close to the primary sensory apparatus of vision, hearing, balance, taste, and smell[WP].

FMA50863.name: cranial nerve II
FMA50863.definition: Cranial nerve fiber tract which is comprised of retinal ganglion cell axons running posterior medially towards the optic chiasm, at which some of the axons cross the midline and after which the structure is termed the optic tract. Transmits visual information from the retina to the brain[ZFA].

FMA50865.name: trochlear nerve
FMA50865.definition: A cranial nerve that runs to the eye muscles.

FMA50872.name: right pulmonary artery
FMA50872.definition: The pulmonary artery that supplies the right lung.

FMA50873.name: left pulmonary artery
FMA50873.definition: The pulmonary artery that supplies the left lung.

FMA51061.name: calcaneal tendon
FMA51061.definition: The Achilles tendon is a tendon of the posterior leg. It serves to attach the plantaris, gastrocnemius (calf) and soleus muscles to the calcaneus (heel) bone.

FMA51071.name: flexor digitorum longus
FMA51071.definition: The Flexor digitorum longus is situated on the tibial side of the leg. At its origin it is thin and pointed, but it gradually increases in size as it descends. This muscle serves to curl the second, third, fourth, and fifth toes (flexion of phalanges II-V). [WP,unvetted].

FMA51099.name: tibialis posterior
FMA51099.definition: The Tibialis posterior is the most central of all the leg muscles, and is located in the posterior compartment of the leg. It is the key stabilizing muscle of the lower leg. [WP,unvetted].

FMA52572.name: superior branch of oculomotor nerve
FMA52572.definition: The superior branch of the oculomotor nerve or the superior division, the smaller, passes medialward over the optic nerve. It supplies the Superior rectus and Levator palpebrae superioris.

FMA52573.name: inferior branch of oculomotor nerve
FMA52573.definition: The inferior branch of the oculomotor nerve or the inferior division, the larger, divides into three branches. One passes beneath the optic nerve to the medial rectus. Another, to the inferior rectus. The third and longest runs forward between the inferior recti and lateralis to the inferior oblique. From the last a short thick branch is given off to the lower part of the ciliary ganglion, and forms its short root.

FMA52621.name: ophthalmic nerve
FMA52621.definition: The sensory nerve subdivision of the trigeminal nerve that transmits sensory information from the orbit and its contents, the nasal cavity and the skin of the nose and forehead.
synonyms: first branch of fifth cranial nerve
first division of fifth cranial nerve

FMA52628.name: lacrimal nerve
FMA52628.definition: The lacrimal nerve is the smallest of the three branches of the ophthalmic division of the trigeminal nerve.

FMA52638.name: frontal nerve (branch of ophthalmic)
FMA52638.definition: The frontal nerve is the largest branch of the ophthalmic, and may be regarded, both from its size and direction, as the continuation of the nerve. It enters the orbit through the supraorbital foramen, and runs forward between the Levator palpebræ superioris and the periosteum. Midway between the apex and base of the orbit it divides into two branches, supratrochlear nerve and supraorbital nerve. [WP,unvetted].

FMA52668.name: nasociliary nerve
FMA52668.definition: A branch of the ophthalmic nerve that serves to supply the mucous membrane of the nose, the tip of the nose, and the conjunctiva.

FMA52691.name: long ciliary nerve
FMA52691.definition: A branch of the nasociliary nerve that innervates the ciliary muscles, the iris, and the cornea.

FMA52734.name: tetrapod frontal bone
FMA52734.definition: The bone forming the forehead and roof of the eye orbit.

FMA52735.name: occipital bone
FMA52735.definition: The bone at the lower, posterior part of the skull.

FMA52736.name: sphenoid bone
FMA52736.definition: An unpaired bone situated at the base of the skull in front of the temporal bone and basilar part of the occipital bone. The sphenoid bone is one of the seven bones that articulate to form the orbit. Its shape somewhat resembles that of a butterfly or bat with its wings extended.

FMA52737.name: temporal bone
FMA52737.definition: The large, irregular bone located at the base and side of the skull; consists of three parts at birth: squamous, tympanic, and petrous.

FMA52740.name: ethmoid bone
FMA52740.definition: A bone in the skull that separates the nasal cavity from the brain. As such, it is located at the roof of the nose, between the two orbits. The cubical bone is lightweight due to a spongy construction. The ethmoid bone is one of the bones that makes up the orbit of the eye[WP].

FMA52741.name: lacrimal bone
FMA52741.definition: The irregularly thin plate that forms part of the medial wall of the orbit behind the frontal process of the maxilla.

FMA52745.name: nasal bone
FMA52745.definition: One of two small oblong bones, varying in size and form in different individuals; they are placed side by side at the middle and upper part of the face, and form, by their junction, 'the bridge' of the nose[WP]. Paired dermal bones, likened to a bone tube, positioned lateral to the supraethmoid.

FMA52746.name: palatine bone
FMA52746.definition: A paired dermal bone situated in the mid-palate that helps form the hard palate [Palaeos].

FMA52747.name: jugal bone
FMA52747.definition: The quadrilateral bone that forms the prominence of the cheek.

FMA52748.name: mandible
FMA52748.definition: A dentary bone that is the only bone in one of the lateral halves of the lower jaw skeleton.

FMA52749.name: hyoid bone
FMA52749.definition: A horseshoe shaped bone situated in the anterior midline of the neck between the chin and the thyroid cartilage. The hyoid bone provides attachment to the muscles of the floor of the mouth and the tongue above, the larynx below, and the epiglottis and pharynx behind. [WP,modified].

FMA52781.name: external ear
FMA52781.definition: Part of the ear external to the tympanum (eardrum). It typically consists of a tube (the external auditory meatus) that directs sound waves on to the tympanum, and may also include the external pinna, which extends beyond the skull[GO].

FMA52801.name: basicranium
FMA52801.definition: The base of skull is the most inferior area of the skull, composed of the endocranium and lower parts of the skull roof.

FMA53667.name: strand of hair
FMA53667.definition: A filament, mostly protein, that grows from follicles found in the dermis[WP].

FMA53672.name: neurocranium
FMA53672.definition: Subdivision of skeletal system that surrounds and protects the brain. Includes the skull base, sensory capsules and the central part of the skull roof.

FMA53673.name: facial skeleton
FMA53673.definition: Subdivision of skull that consists of the facial bones.

FMA54237.name: eyebrow
FMA54237.definition: The eyebrow is an area of thick, delicate hairs above the eye that follows the shape of the lower margin of the brow ridges. Their main function is to protect the eye, but they are also important to human communication and facial expression. It is not uncommon for people to modify their eyebrows by means of hair addition or removal, make up, or piercings.

FMA54241.name: hair of head
FMA54241.definition: A strand of hair that is part of a head.

FMA54250.name: hair of trunk
FMA54250.definition: A strand of hair that is part of a trunk.

FMA54319.name: strand of pubic hair
FMA54319.definition: A hair in the frontal genital area of adolescent and adult humans, located on and around the sex organs, the crotch, and sometimes at the top of the inside of the thighs, in the pubic region around the pubis bone.

FMA54375.name: nasal septum
FMA54375.definition: The nasal septum separates the left and right airways in the nose, dividing the two nostrils. It is depressed by the Depressor septi nasi muscle. [WP,unvetted].

FMA54397.name: skeleton of upper jaw
FMA54397.definition: A subdivision of the skeleton that corresponds to the upper part of the mouth. The lower jaw skeleton includes the following elements, when present: upper jaw teeth, the maxilla and other lower jaw bones.

FMA54398.name: skeleton of lower jaw
FMA54398.definition: A subdivision of the skeleton that corresponds to the lower part of the mouth. The lower jaw skeleton includes the following elements, when present: lower jaw teeth, the mandible and other lower jaw bones, and Meckel's cartilage.

FMA54640.name: tongue
FMA54640.definition: A muscular organ in the floor of the mouth.

FMA54736.name: inferior nasal concha
FMA54736.definition: A turbinal located on the maxilla bone.

FMA55021.name: soft palate
FMA55021.definition: The muscular, non-bony arch-shaped posterior portion of the palate extending from the posterior edge of the hard palate.

FMA55022.name: palatine uvula
FMA55022.definition: Conic projection from the posterior edge of the middle of the soft palate, composed of connective tissue containing a number of racemose glands, and some muscular fibers.

FMA55077.name: pharyngeal raphe
FMA55077.definition: The Pharyngeal raphe is a raphe that serves as the origin and insertion for several of the pharyngeal constrictors.

FMA55093.name: submandibular gland
FMA55093.definition: Either of the paired compound tubuloalveolar (aka tubuloacinar) major salivary glands composed of both serous and mucous secretory cells and situated beneath the mandible.

FMA55099.name: thyroid cartilage
FMA55099.definition: The largest of the laryngeal cartilages.

FMA55107.name: cartilage element
FMA55107.definition: Skeletal element that is composed of cartilage tissue and may be permanent or transient.

FMA55108.name: laryngeal cartilage
FMA55108.definition: The cartilaginous structures that support the larynx.

FMA55109.name: arytenoid cartilage
FMA55109.definition: The paired triangular laryngeal cartilages located postlaterally at the level of the thyroid cartilage.

FMA55110.name: corniculate cartilage
FMA55110.definition: The corniculate cartilages (cartilages of Santorini) are two small conical nodules consisting of yellow elastic cartilage, which articulate with the summits of the arytenoid cartilages and serve to prolong them posteriorly and medially. They are situated in the posterior parts of the aryepiglottic folds of mucous membrane, and are sometimes fused with the arytenoid cartilages. [WP,unvetted].

FMA55111.name: cuneiform cartilage
FMA55111.definition: The cuneiform cartilages of the larynx are two small, elongated pieces of yellow elastic cartilage, placed one on either side, in the aryepiglottic fold, where they give rise to small whitish elevations on the surface of the mucous membrane, just in front of the arytenoid cartilages.

FMA55130.name: epiglottis
FMA55130.definition: A part of the pharynx that consists of a flap of elastic cartilage tissue plus a mucous membrane covering, attached to the entrance of the larynx. The epiglottis is found at the root of the tongue and folds back over the entrance to the larynx during swallowing, preventing inhalation of food or drink[MP,modified].

FMA55131.name: ligament of larynx
FMA55131.definition: A ligament that is part of a larynx and connexts the cartilages of the larynx.

FMA55138.name: median thyrohyoid ligament
FMA55138.definition: The middle thicker part of the thyrohyoid membrane is termed the median thyrohyoid ligament (middle hyothyroid ligament, middle thyrohyoid ligament), its lateral thinner portions are pierced by the superior laryngeal vessels and the internal branch of the superior laryngeal nerve. Its anterior surface is in relation with the Thyreohyoideus, Sternohyoideus, and Omohyoideus, and with the body of the hyoid bone.

FMA55139.name: lateral thyrohyoid ligament
FMA55139.definition: The lateral thyrohyoid ligament (lateral hyothyroid ligament) is a round elastic cord, which forms the posterior border of the hyothyroid membrane and passes between the tip of the superior cornu of the thyroid cartilage and the extremity of the greater cornu of the hyoid bone. The recurrent laryngeal nerve typical lies lateral to this ligament.

FMA55227.name: hyoepiglottic ligament
FMA55227.definition: An elastic band connecting the anterior surface of the epiglottis to the upper border of the body of the hyoid bone.

FMA55230.name: thyroepiglottic ligament
FMA55230.definition: Laryngeal ligament that connects the epiglottis to the thyroid cartilage[WP,modified].

FMA55233.name: cricothyroid ligament
FMA55233.definition: This attaches the caudal border of the thyroid cartilage to the ventral arch of the cricoid cartilage. Its sheetlike ventral portion is sometimes referred to as the cricothyroid membrane. Being elastic, it 'balances' movement at the hinge-like cricothyroid joint and determines the resting position of the larynx when the muscles are relaxed[MURDOCH].

FMA55618.name: pterygomandibular raphe
FMA55618.definition: The pterygomandibular raphe (pterygomandibular ligament) is a tendinous band of the buccopharyngeal fascia, attached by one extremity to the hamulus of the medial pterygoid plate, and by the other to the posterior end of the mylohyoid line of the mandible. Its medial surface is covered by the mucous membrane of the mouth.

FMA55636.name: cuspid
FMA55636.definition: A tooth that is typically long and pointed and bearing a single cusp.

FMA55637.name: premolar tooth
FMA55637.definition: The premolar teeth or bicuspids are transitional teeth located between the canine and molar teeth.

FMA55638.name: molar tooth
FMA55638.definition: Molars are the rearmost and most complicated kind of tooth in most mammals.

FMA55670.name: solid compound organ
FMA55670.definition: Compound organ that does not contain macroscopic anatomical spaces.

FMA55671.name: cavitated compound organ
FMA55671.definition: Compound organ that contains one or more macroscopic anatomical spaces.

FMA55675.name: central nervous system
FMA55675.definition: The central nervous system is the core nervous system that serves an integrating and coordinating function. In vertebrates it consists of the neural tube derivatives: the brain and spinal cord. In invertebrates it includes central ganglia plus nerve cord.

FMA55676.name: regional part of brain
FMA55676.definition: Anatomical divisons of the brain according to one or more criteria, e.g. cytoarchitectural, gross anatomy. Parts may be contiguous in 3D or not, e.g., basal ganglia.

FMA55714.name: upper secondary canine tooth
FMA55714.definition: A secondary canine tooth that is part of a upper jaw region.

FMA55715.name: lower secondary canine tooth
FMA55715.definition: A secondary canine tooth that is part of a lower jaw region.

FMA55720.name: upper secondary molar tooth
FMA55720.definition: A secondary molar tooth that is part of a upper jaw region.

FMA55721.name: lower secondary molar tooth
FMA55721.definition: A secondary molar tooth that is part of a lower jaw region.

FMA55723.name: lower central secondary incisor tooth
FMA55723.definition: A lower jaw incisor that is in_the_central_side_of a dentition.

FMA55725.name: lower lateral secondary incisor tooth
FMA55725.definition: A lower jaw incisor that is in_the_lateral_side_of a dentition.

FMA58071.name: chamber of eyeball
FMA58071.definition: A segment of the eyeball that is filled with refractive media.

FMA58078.name: anterior chamber of eyeball
FMA58078.definition: The space in the eye, filled with aqueous humor, and bounded anteriorly by the cornea and a small portion of the sclera and posteriorly by a small portion of the ciliary body, the iris, and part of the crystalline lens.

FMA58102.name: tunica fibrosa of eyeball
FMA58102.definition: The sclera and cornea form the fibrous tunic of the bulb of the eye; the sclera is opaque, and constitutes the posterior five-sixths of the tunic; the cornea is transparent, and forms the anterior sixth.

FMA58235.name: iris
FMA58235.definition: The adjustable membrane, composed of the stroma and pigmented epithelium, located just in front of the crystalline lens within the eye.

FMA58238.name: cornea
FMA58238.definition: The transparent anterior portion of the fibrous coat of the eye that serves as the chief refractory structure.

FMA58241.name: lens of camera-type eye
FMA58241.definition: A transparent and refractive lens located posterior to the iris. The lens of camera-type eye refracts light to be focused on the retina.

FMA58245.name: lacrimal canaliculus
FMA58245.definition: The part of the lacrimal duct that connects the lacrimal punctum to the lacrimal sac.

FMA58269.name: sclera
FMA58269.definition: Opaque fibrous outer layer of the eyeball[ZFA,Kardong,WP].

FMA58274.name: skeletal muscle of trunk
FMA58274.definition: A skeletal muscle organ that is part of the trunk region.

FMA58298.name: optic choroid
FMA58298.definition: Vascular layer containing connective tissue, of the eye lying between the retina and the sclera. The choroid provides oxygen and nourishment to the outer layers of the retina. Along with the ciliary body and iris, the choroid forms the uveal tract[WP].

FMA58431.name: pars plicata of ciliary body
FMA58431.definition: Corrugated anterior region of ciliary body where ciliary processes arise.

FMA5865.name: cranial nerve
FMA5865.definition: Cranial nerves are nerves that emerge directly from the brain, in contrast to spinal nerves, which emerge from segments of the spinal cord.

FMA58827.name: vitreous body
FMA58827.definition: Gelatinous mucoid tissue that is composed of vitreous humor and fills the cavity behind the crystalline lens of the eye and in front of the retina[MP,modified].

FMA58838.name: suspensory ligament of lens
FMA58838.definition: The zonule of Zinn (Zinn's membrane, ciliary zonule) is a ring of fibrous strands connecting the ciliary body with the crystalline lens of the eye. The zonule of Zinn is split into two layers: a thin layer, which lines the hyaloid fossa, and a thicker layer, which is a collection of zonular fibers. Together, the fibers are known as the suspensory ligament of the lens[WP].

FMA5884.name: ganglion
FMA5884.definition: A biological tissue mass, most commonly a mass of nerve cell bodies.

FMA5889.name: autonomic ganglion
FMA5889.definition: Ganglion that has dendrites that form a junction between autonomic nerves originating from the central nervous system and autonomic nerves innervating their target organs in the periphery. There are two subtypes, sympathetic ganglion and parasympathetic ganglion.

FMA5894.name: parasympathetic ganglion
FMA5894.definition: Ganglion containing neurons that receive innervation from parasympathetic neurons in the central nervous system and subserves parasympathetic functions through innervation of smooth muscle, cardiac muscle and glands.

FMA5897.name: anatomical space
FMA5897.definition: Non-material anatomical entity of three dimensions, that is generated by morphogenetic or other physiologic processes; is surrounded by one or more anatomical structures; contains one or more organism substances or anatomical structures.

FMA5898.name: anatomical junction
FMA5898.definition: An anatomical structure that connects two structures.

FMA59086.name: eyelid tarsus
FMA59086.definition: The tarsi (tarsal plates) are two comparatively thick, elongated plates of dense connective tissue, about 2.5 cm. in length; one is found in each eyelid, and contributes to its form and support. They directly abut the lid margins.

FMA59101.name: lacrimal gland
FMA59101.definition: The lacrimal glands are paired almond-shaped glands, located in or near the orbital region, that secrete the aqueous layer of the tear film.[WP].

FMA59398.name: lower jaw region
FMA59398.definition: Subdivision of head that consists of the lower jaw skeletal elements plus associated soft tissue (skin, lips, muscle)[cjm].

FMA59399.name: upper jaw region
FMA59399.definition: Subdivision of head that consists of the upper jaw skeletal elements plus associated soft tissue (skin, lips, muscle)[cjm].

FMA59402.name: lacrimal lake
FMA59402.definition: A small cistern-like area of the conjunctiva at the medial angle of the eye, in which the tears collect after bathing the front surface of the eyeball and the conjunctival sac.

FMA59502.name: nasal cartilage
FMA59502.definition: One of the cartilage structures in the nose that provide form and support[WP].

FMA59504.name: major alar cartilage
FMA59504.definition: The greater alar cartilage (lower lateral cartilage) is a thin, flexible plate, situated immediately below the preceding, and bent upon itself in such a manner as to form the medial wall and lateral wall of the naris of its own side.

FMA59511.name: lateral nasal cartilage
FMA59511.definition: The lateral cartilage (upper lateral cartilage) is situated below the inferior margin of the nasal bone, and is flattened, and triangular in shape.[WP].

FMA59515.name: external nose
FMA59515.definition: External part of the nose containing the external nares.

FMA59517.name: dorsum of nose
FMA59517.definition: The midline prominence of the nose, extending from the nasal root to the tip.

FMA59762.name: gingiva
FMA59762.definition: The fibrous investing tissue, covered by keratinized epithelium, that immediately surrounds a tooth and is contiguous with its periodontal ligament and with the mucosal tissues of the mouth[Glossary of Periodontal Terms 2001].

FMA59763.name: gingiva of upper jaw
FMA59763.definition: A gingiva that is part of a upper jaw region.

FMA59764.name: gingiva of lower jaw
FMA59764.definition: A gingiva that is part of a lower jaw region.

FMA59788.name: major salivary gland
FMA59788.definition: One of the three largest glands of the oral cavity that secrete most of the saliva, including the parotid, submandibular, and sublingual glands.

FMA59791.name: sublingual gland
FMA59791.definition: The small mucin-producing salivary glands in the floor of the mouth beneath the tongue, anterior to the submandibular gland.

FMA59816.name: lip
FMA59816.definition: One of the two fleshy folds which surround the opening of the mouth.

FMA60116.name: nasal skeleton
FMA60116.definition: Structural framework that provides support to the nasal sacs and ducts.

FMA61681.name: lower back
FMA61681.definition: Subdivision of abdominal segment of trunk which in humans is demarcated from the front of the abdomen by the posterior surface of the anterior layer of the thoracolumbar fascia and the anterior surface of the lumbar vertebral column; together with the front of the abdomen, it constitutes the abdomen[Modified from FMA].

FMA61819.name: left cerebral hemisphere
FMA61819.definition: A cerebral hemisphere that is in the left side of a brain.

FMA61823.name: lobe of cerebral hemisphere
FMA61823.definition: Subdivision of telencephalon which is one of a number of subdivisions of each hemisphere separated by both real landmarks (sulci and fissures) and arbitrary boundaries[FMA,modified].

FMA61833.name: caudate nucleus
FMA61833.definition: Subcortical nucleus of telecephalic origin consisting of an elongated gray mass lying lateral to and bordering the lateral ventricle. It is divided into a head, body and tail in some species.

FMA61834.name: putamen
FMA61834.definition: Subcortical nucleus of telencephalic , which together with the caudate nucleus, forms the striatum. The putamen lies lateral to the internal capsule and medial to the external medullary lamina, and is separated from the caudate nucleus by the fibers of the internal capsule for most of its length, except at its anterior portion.

FMA61835.name: globus pallidus
FMA61835.definition: Subcortical nucleus, functionally part of the basal ganglia, which consists of two segments the external (or lateral) and internal (or medial) separated by the medial medullary lamina in primates. In rodents, The globus pallidus lateral is separated from the medial segment by the fibers of the internal capsule/cerebral peduncle.

FMA61841.name: amygdala
FMA61841.definition: Subcortical brain region lying anterior to the hippocampal formation in the temporal lobe and anterior to the temporal horn of the lateral ventricle in some species. It is usually subdivided into several groups. Functionally, it is not considered a unitary structure (MM).

FMA61842.name: septum of telencephalon
FMA61842.definition: Gray matter structure located on the midline of the forebrain consisting of the septum pellucidum (in some species) and the septal nuclei (Heimer, 1996).

FMA61857.name: superior frontal gyrus
FMA61857.definition: Component of the frontal lobe, lateral aspect. The rostral boundary is the first appearance of the superior frontal sulcus whereas the caudal boundary is the midpoint of the paracentral sulcus on the 'inflated' surface. The medial and lateral boundaries are the medial aspect of the frontal lobe and the superior frontal sulcus respectively (Christine Fennema-Notestine).

FMA61859.name: middle frontal gyrus
FMA61859.definition: Component of the frontal lobe, lateral aspect (Christine Fennema-Notestine).

FMA61860.name: inferior frontal gyrus
FMA61860.definition: Component of the frontal lobe, lateral aspect. The rostral boundary is the first appearance of the inferior frontal sulcus whereas the caudal boundary is the precentral gyrus. The medial and lateral boundaries are the lateral bank of the inferior frontal sulcus and the medial bank of the lateral orbital sulcus and/or the circular insular sulcus respectively (Christein Fennema-Notestine).

FMA61894.name: precentral gyrus
FMA61894.definition: Component of the frontal lobe. The appearance and disappearance of the central sulcus is the rostral and caudal boundaries of the precentral gyrus respectively. The medial boundary is specific frontal gyri (superior, middle and inferior) whereas the lateral boundary is the medial bank of the central sulcus (Christine Fennema-Notestine).

FMA61896.name: postcentral gyrus
FMA61896.definition: Component of the parietal lobe. The appearance and disappearance of the central sulcus were the rostral and caudal boundaries of the postcentral gyrus respectively. The medial and lateral boundaries were the lateral bank of the precentral gyrus and the lateral fissure and/or the medial bank of the superior parietal gyrus respectively (Christine Fennema-Notestine).

FMA61897.name: supramarginal gyrus
