FMA61897.definition: Component of the parietal lobe. The first coronal slice between the superior temporal gyrus and the postcentral gyrus where the supramarginal gyrus appears was the rostral boundary whereas the slice where the supramarginal gyrus becomes continuous with the superior parietal gyrus was the caudal boundary.
synonyms: anterior part of inferior parietal lobule

FMA61898.name: angular gyrus
FMA61898.definition: Part of inferior parietal lobule formed by the cortex surrounding the upturned end of the superior temporal sulcus (Nolte, The Human Brain, 6th ed, 2009, pg 659).
synonyms: middle part of inferior parietal lobule

FMA61899.name: superior parietal cortex
FMA61899.definition: Copmonent of the parietal lobe. The rostral and caudal boundaries of the superior parietal cortex were the precentral gyrus and lateral occipital cortex respectively. The medial and lateral boundaries were the precuneus and/or cuneus cortex and the infererior parietal cortex respectively (Christine Fennema-Notestine).

FMA61906.name: middle temporal gyrus
FMA61906.definition: Component of the temporal lobe, lateral aspect. The rostral boundary is the rostral extent of the superior temporal sulcus whereas the caudal boundary is the temporo-occipital incisure on the cortical surface. The superior temporal sulcus is the medial boundary and the inferior temporal sulcus is the lateral boundary (Christine Fennema-Notestine).

FMA61907.name: inferior temporal gyrus
FMA61907.definition: Component of the temporal lobe, lateral aspect. The rostral boundary is the rostral extent of the inferior temporal sulcus whereas the caudal boundary is designated as the temporo-occipital incisure on the cortical surface. The occipitotemporal sulcus is the medial boundary and the inferior temporal sulcus is the lateral boundary (Christine Fennema-Notestine).

FMA61908.name: fusiform gyrus
FMA61908.definition: The fusiform gyrus is part of the temporal lobe. It is also known as the (discontinuous) occipitotemporal gyrus. Other sources have the fusiform gyrus above the occipitotemporal gyrus and underneath the parahippocampal gyrus. [WP,unvetted].

FMA61918.name: parahippocampal gyrus
FMA61918.definition: Component of the temporal lobe on the mesial surface, posterior to the entorhinal cortex. The rostral and caudal boundaries are the posterior end of the netorhinal cortex and the caudal portion of the hippocampus, respectively. The medial boudnary is designated as the medial aspect off the temporal lobe and the lateral boundary is the collateral sulcus (Christine Fennema-Notestine).

FMA61934.name: choroid plexus
FMA61934.definition: A network formed by blood vessels and the tela choroidea which secretes CSF into the ventricular spaces.

FMA61950.name: internal capsule of telencephalon
FMA61950.definition: White matter regional part of brain which is flanked by nuclear masses, consisting of both afferent and efferent fibers projecting between the cerebral cortex and the brainstem and spinal cord. It consists of three distinct parts: an anterior limb, posterior limb, and genu. (Adapted from MSH by Maryann Martone).

FMA61961.name: anterior commissure
FMA61961.definition: A bundle of myelinated nerve fibers passing transversely through the lamina terminalis and connecting symmetrical parts of the two cerebral hemispheres; it consists of a smaller anterior part (pars anterior commissurae anterioris) and a larger posterior part (pars posterior commissurae anterioris).

FMA61965.name: fornix of brain
FMA61965.definition: A C-shaped bundle of fibres (axons) in the brain, and carries signals from the hippocampus to the mammillary bodies and septal nuclei. It is typically divided into the columns (crus), body, commissure and the pre-commissural and post-commissural fornix (MM).

FMA61970.name: hippocampal commissure
FMA61970.definition: The triangular subcallosal plate of commissural fibers resulting from the converging of the right and left fornix bundles which exchange numerous fibers and which curve back in the contralateral fornix to end in the hippocampus of the opposite side.

FMA61974.name: stria terminalis
FMA61974.definition: White matter structure in the brain consisting of fibers running along the lateral margin of the ventricular surface of the thalamus. The stria terminalis covers the thalamostriate vein, marking a line of separation between the thalamus and the caudate nucleus as seen upon gross dissection of the ventricles of the brain, viewed from the superior aspect.

FMA61975.name: lamina terminalis of cerebral hemisphere
FMA61975.definition: The remnant of the lamina terminalis in the developed brain.

FMA61992.name: forebrain
FMA61992.definition: The most anterior region of the brain including both the telencephalon and diencephalon.

FMA61993.name: midbrain
FMA61993.definition: The midbrain is the middle division of the three primary divisions of the developing chordate brain or the corresponding part of the adult brain (in vertebrates, includes a ventral part containing the cerebral peduncles and a dorsal tectum containing the corpora quadrigemina and that surrounds the aqueduct of Sylvius connecting the third and fourth ventricles)[GO].

FMA61996.name: prosomere
FMA61996.definition: A neuromere that is part of the presumptive forebrain.

FMA61997.name: midbrain neuromere
FMA61997.definition: A neuromere that is part of the presumptive midbrain.

FMA62000.name: telencephalon
FMA62000.definition: Part of the forebrain consisting of paired olfactory bulbs and cerebral hemispheres.

FMA62001.name: diencephalon
FMA62001.definition: The division of the forebrain that develops from the foremost primary cerebral vesicle.

FMA62003.name: metencephalon
FMA62003.definition: Rostral segment of the hindbrain that has as its parts the pons (where present) and the cerebellum[WP,modified].

FMA62004.name: medulla oblongata
FMA62004.definition: Organ component of neuraxis that has as its parts the medullary reticular formation, inferior olivary complex and cochlear nuclear complex, among other structures[FMA]. The medulla oblongata lies directly above the spinal cord and controls vital autonomic functions such as digestion, breathing and the control of heart rate[GO].

FMA62008.name: hypothalamus
FMA62008.definition: A specialized brain region of the ventral diencephalon arising near the end of the segmentation period; the embryonic hypothalamic region will give rise to the posterior pituitary gland as well as a number of brain nuclei. [ZFA]. One of the most important functions of the hypothalamus is to link the nervous system to the endocrine system via the pituitary gland (hypophysis).[Wikipedia].

FMA62009.name: epithalamus
FMA62009.definition: Most dorsal part of the thalamus, comprising the pineal gland and habenular nuclei in most vertebrates. In a few vertebrates, it also includes the parietal eye. (Butler and Hodos, Comparative Vertebrate Neuroanatomy, 2nd ed, 2005, pg. 345-346.

FMA62028.name: intermediate hypothalamic region
FMA62028.definition: The portion of the hypothalamus located generally internal to the region of the infundibulum.

FMA62032.name: habenula
FMA62032.definition: A segment of the epithalamus that has as its parts the habenular nuclei and the habenular commissure[FMA,modified].

FMA62033.name: pineal body
FMA62033.definition: A midline, cone like structure located in the dorso-caudal roof of the 3rd ventricle, attached by peduncles to the habenular and posterior commissures. The stalk contains nerve fibers, blood vessels, connective tissue and parenchymal cells (Paxinos, The Rat Central Nervous System, 2nd ed, pg 399).

FMA62045.name: optic chiasma
FMA62045.definition: A decussation of the diencephalon where the fibers of the optic nerve cross.

FMA62046.name: optic tract
FMA62046.definition: Diencephalic white matter (tract) which is comprised of retinal ganglion cell axons after which they have passed through the optic chiasm[ZFA]. Predominantly white matter structure found in diencephalon consisting of fibers originating in the retina. The optic tract is considered to extend from the point of the optic chiasm and terminates largely, although not exclusively, in the lateral geniculate complex.

FMA62072.name: posterior commissure
FMA62072.definition: Rounded band of white fibers crossing the middle line on the dorsal aspect of the upper end of the cerebral aqueduct. It is important in the bilateral pupillary light reflex. Its fibers acquire their medullary sheaths early, but their connections have not been definitely determined.

FMA62080.name: stria medullaris
FMA62080.definition: The major afferent track to the habenula from the telencephalon (particularly in the septal side) in all vertebrates[Butler and Hodos].

FMA62209.name: lateral geniculate body
FMA62209.definition: The group of neurons that serve as the primary processor of visual information received from the retina via the optic tract and send processed information to the visual cortex of the occipital lobe.

FMA62211.name: medial geniculate body
FMA62211.definition: Nuclear complex of the thalamus situated on the caudal, subpial aspect of the thalamus (Brodal, Neurological Anatomy, 3rd ed., 1981, pg 622).

FMA62327.name: tuber cinereum
FMA62327.definition: Part of hypothalamus consisting of hollow eminence of gray matter situated between the mammilary bodies and the optic chiasm visible on the basal surface of the brain (adapted from Wikipedia).

FMA62394.name: cerebral peduncle
FMA62394.definition: Synonym for macrodissected adult human tegmentum (Vicq d'Azyr, 1784; Swanson, 2000); pp. 555-556. Later used thus by for example His (1893b, p. 178), Herrick (1915, p. 160), Strong & Elwyn (1943, p. 17), Carpenter (1976, p. 367), Williams & Warwick (1980, p. 935).

FMA62403.name: superior colliculus
FMA62403.definition: Part of the midbrain tecturm consisting of paired bodies that sit caudal to the thalamus and surround the pineal gland in the mesencephalon of vertebrate brains. It comprises the rostral aspect of the midbrain, posterior to the periaqueductal gray and adjacent superior the inferior colliculus. The inferior and superior colliculi are known collectively as the corpora quadrigemina (Latin, quadruplet bodies).

FMA62404.name: inferior colliculus
FMA62404.definition: Part of the midbrain tectum, consisting of paired predominantly gray matter elevations on the dorsal aspect of the midbrain, located caudal to the superior colliculus, dorsal to the periaqueductal gray of the cerebral aqueduct and rostral to the cerebellum.

FMA62434.name: cingulate gyrus
FMA62434.definition: One of the convolutions on the medial surface of the cerebral hemisphere. It surrounds the rostral part of the brain and interhemispheric commissure and forms part of the limbic system. (MSH) One of three essential structures comprising the limbic lobe, the other two being the hippocampus and parahippocampal gyrus. (CSP).

FMA62445.name: commissure of diencephalon
FMA62445.definition: A commissure that is part of a diencephalon.

FMA62493.name: Ammon's horn
FMA62493.definition: A part of the brain consisting of a three layered cortex located in the forebrain bordering the medial surface of the lateral ventricle. The term hippocampus is often used synonymously with hippocampal formation which consists of the hippocampus proper or Cornu Ammonis, the dentate gyrus and the subiculum.

FMA62514.name: basal ganglion
FMA62514.definition: An individual member of a collection of basal ganglia. Basal ganglia are subcortical masses of gray matter in the forebrain and midbrain that are richly interconnected and so viewed as a functional system. The nuclei usually included are the caudate nucleus (caudoputamen in rodents), putamen, globus pallidus, substantia nigra (pars compacta and pars reticulata) and the subthalamic nucleus.

FMA62955.name: anatomical entity
FMA62955.definition: Biological entity that is either an individual member of a biological species or constitutes the structural organization of an individual member of a biological species.

FMA64829.name: scalene muscle
FMA64829.definition: Any of the three pairs of muscles in the lateral neck, namely the scalenus anterior, scalenus medius, and scalenus posterior. They are innervated by the spinal nerves C4-C8[WP].

FMA64916.name: thenar muscle
FMA64916.definition: Any of the muscles of the thenar eminence, a raised fleshy area on the palm of the hand near the base of the thumb.

FMA64917.name: hypothenar muscle
FMA64917.definition: Any of three muscles of the palm that control the motion of the little finger.

FMA64922.name: gluteal muscle
FMA64922.definition: On of the muscles that make up the buttocks: the gluteus maximus muscle, gluteus medius muscle and gluteus minimus muscle.

FMA65020.name: intrinsic muscle of pes
FMA65020.definition: Any of the intrinsic muscles of the pes (foot).

FMA65132.name: nerve
FMA65132.definition: An enclosed, cable-like bundle of axons in the peripheral nervous system originating in a nerve root in the central nervous system (or a condensed nervous structure) connecting with peripheral structures.

FMA66320.name: thoracodorsal artery
FMA66320.definition: The thoracodorsal artery is a branch of the subscapular artery. It travels inferiorly with the thoracodorsal nerve and supplies the latissimus dorsi. [WP,unvetted].

FMA66326.name: pulmonary artery
FMA66326.definition: An artery that carries deoxygenated blood from heart to the lungs. They are the only arteries (other than umbilical arteries in the fetus) that carry deoxygenated blood..

FMA66464.name: systemic artery
FMA66464.definition: An artery of the systemic circulation, which is the part of the cardiovascular system which carries oxygenated blood away from the heart, to the body, and returns deoxygenated blood back to the heart.

FMA66643.name: pulmonary vein
FMA66643.definition: Pulmonary veins are blood vessels that transport blood from the lungs to the heart[GO].

FMA66644.name: systemic vein
FMA66644.definition: Any vein within the general circulation that transports blood back to the right atrium of the heart.

FMA66645.name: portal vein
FMA66645.definition: A vein that conducts blood from the digestive organs, spleen, pancreas, and gallbladder to the liver[BTO].

FMA67112.name: immaterial anatomical entity
FMA67112.definition: Anatomical entity that has no mass.

FMA67135.name: anatomical structure
FMA67135.definition: Material anatomical entity that is a single connected structure with inherent 3D shape generated by coordinated expression of the organism's own genome.

FMA67242.name: gray matter
FMA67242.definition: A nervous system structure composed primarily of nerve cell bodies (somas). May also include dendrites and the initial unmyelinated portion of axons.

FMA67292.name: right cerebral hemisphere
FMA67292.definition: A cerebral hemisphere that is in the right side of a brain.

FMA67325.name: occipital lobe
FMA67325.definition: Posterior part of the cerebral hemisphere (MSH).

FMA67329.name: insula
FMA67329.definition: Gray matter of the insular region of the neocortex. In gyrencephalic animals, it is part of the insular lobe and lies in the depths of the lateral fissure and covered by portions of the frontal, parietal and temporal lobes. It includes Brodmann areas 13-16.

FMA67498.name: organ
FMA67498.definition: Anatomical structure that performs a specific function or group of functions [WP].

FMA67552.name: anatomical cavity
FMA67552.definition: Anatomical space which contains portions of one or more body substances and is bounded by the internal surface of one maximally connected anatomical structure. Examples: cranial cavity, pharyngeal recess space, nasal cavity, tooth socket, cavity of serous sac, lumen of stomach, lumen of artery, fornix of vagina.

FMA67601.name: anatomical projection
FMA67601.definition: A projection or outgrowth of tissue from a larger body or organ.

FMA67687.name: hindbrain
FMA67687.definition: The most posterior of the three principal regions of the brain. In mammals and birds the hindbrain is divided into a rostral metencephalon and a caudal myelencephalon. In zebrafish, with the exception of the cerebellum, the ventral remainder of the metencephalon can be separated only arbitrarily from the more caudal myelencephalic portion of the medulla oblongata (From: Neuroanatomy of the Zebrafish Brain)[ZFA].

FMA67943.name: pons
FMA67943.definition: The part of the central nervous system lying between the medulla oblongata and the midbrain, ventral to the cerebellum.

FMA67944.name: cerebellum
FMA67944.definition: Part of the metencephalon that lies in the posterior cranial fossa behind the brain stem. It is concerned with the coordination of movement[MESH]. A large dorsally projecting part of the brain concerned especially with the coordination of muscles and the maintenance of bodily equilibrium, situated between the brain stem and the back of the cerebrum , and formed in humans of two lateral lobes and a median lobe[BTO].

FMA67950.name: stria of telencephalon
FMA67950.definition: A stria of neuraxis that is part of a telencephalon.

FMA67951.name: white matter lamina of cerebral hemisphere

FMA68068.name: inferior phrenic vein
FMA68068.definition: The Inferior Phrenic Veins drain the diaphragm and follow the course of the inferior phrenic arteries; the right ends in the inferior vena cava; the left is often represented by two branches, one of which ends in the left renal or suprarenal vein, while the other passes in front of the esophageal hiatus in the diaphragm and opens into the inferior vena cava. [WP,unvetted].

FMA68109.name: bronchial artery
FMA68109.definition: A systemic artery that supplies the lung with with oxygenated blood.

FMA69264.name: inferior suprarenal artery
FMA69264.definition: Each renal artery gives off some small inferior suprarenal branches to the suprarenal gland, the ureter, and the surrounding cellular tissue and muscles. [WP,unvetted].

FMA6964.name: main ciliary ganglion
FMA6964.definition: A parasympathetic ganglion located in the posterior orbit that contains preganglionic nerves and postganglionic neurons of the oculomotor nerve, connects to the Edinger-Westphal nucleus via the oculomotor nerve and the eye muscles via the short ciliary nerve.

FMA70248.name: femoral artery
FMA70248.definition: The femoral artery is a large artery in the muscles of the thigh. It is a continuation of external iliac artery where it enters the femoral triangle at the mid inguinal point behind the inguinal ligament. It leaves femoral triangle through apex beneath the sartorius muscle.

FMA7041.name: short ciliary nerve
FMA7041.definition: A branch of the ciliary ganglion that innervates the ciliary muscles, the iris, and the tunics of the eyeball.

FMA70437.name: superior pancreaticoduodenal artery
FMA70437.definition: The superior pancreaticoduodenal artery is an artery that supplies blood to the duodenum and pancreas. It is a branch of the gastroduodenal artery, which comes from the common hepatic artery of the celiac trunk. The common hepatic itself becomes the proper hepatic after giving off the gastroduodenal artery and goes on to supply the right and left lobes of the liver.

FMA70447.name: right artery of caudate lobe
FMA70447.definition: An artery that branches from the right hepatic artery and supplies the lateral portion of the caudate lobe of the liver.
synonyms: Caudate lobe branch of right hepatic artery

FMA70455.name: left artery of caudate lobe
FMA70455.definition: An artery that branches from the left hepatic artery and supplies the medial portion of the caudate lobe of the liver.
synonyms: Caudate lobe branch of left hepatic artery

FMA70479.name: anterior inferior pancreaticoduodenal artery
FMA70479.definition: An artery that branches from the inferior pancreaticoduodenal artery. It courses on the anterior surface of the uncinate process continuing on to the head of the pancreas. It supplies the uncinate process, head of the pancreas, and the second and third parts of the duodenum.

FMA70480.name: posterior inferior pancreaticoduodenal artery
FMA70480.definition: An artery that branches from the inferior pancreaticoduodenal artery. It courses posterior to the uncinate process and head of the pancreas. It supplies uncinate process and head of the pancreas, second and third parts of the duodenum.

FMA70491.name: ureteric segment of renal artery
FMA70491.definition: The ureteral branches of renal artery are small branches which supply the ureter.

FMA70494.name: segmental renal artery
FMA70494.definition: An artery that branches from the renal artery. The anterior division of the renal artery typically divides into four segmental arteries, whereas the posterior division of the renal artery supplies one segmental artery.

FMA70499.name: superior segmental renal artery
FMA70499.definition: A segmental renal artery that passes anterior to the renal pelvis, superiorly and laterally. It supplies the superior (apical) lobe of the kidney.

FMA70502.name: inferior segmental renal artery
FMA70502.definition: A segmental renal artery that passes anterior to the renal pelvis, inferiorly and laterally towards the inferior pole of the kidney. It supplies the inferior lobe of the kidney, which encompasses the whole of the inferior pole of the kidney, including the anterior and posterior surfaces.

FMA70503.name: posterior segmental renal artery
FMA70503.definition: A segmental renal artery that passes posterior to the renal pelvis and travels laterally, more or less horizontally. It supplies the posterior lobe of the kidney, which includes all of the central-posterior surface of the kidney. This excludes the superior and inferior poles and a small posterolateral portion.

FMA70504.name: carotid artery segment
FMA70504.definition: One of: the common carotid artery, or its branches, the external and internal carotid arteries.

FMA70741.name: collection of hair on face
FMA70741.definition: A collection of hairs that is part of a face.

FMA70752.name: collection of hairs
FMA70752.definition: An anatomical cluster that composed_primarily_of a strand of hair.

FMA70800.name: dorsal metacarpal artery
FMA70800.definition: Aanastomosis of dorsal carpal branch of the radial artery and the dorsal carpal branch of the ulnar artery near the back of the wrist. It is made up of the dorsal carpal branches of both the ulnar and radial arteries. It also anastomoses with the anterior interosseous artery and the posterior interosseous artery. The arch gives off three dorsal metacarpal arteries.

FMA7088.name: heart
FMA7088.definition: A myogenic muscular circulatory organ found in the vertebrate cardiovascular system composed of chambers of cardiac muscle. It is the primary circulatory organ.

FMA7096.name: right cardiac atrium
FMA7096.definition: A cardiac atrium that is in the right side of the heart. It receives deoxygenated blood. In mammals, this comes from the superior and inferior vena cava and the coronary sinus, and pumps it into the right ventricle through the tricuspid valve.

FMA7097.name: left cardiac atrium
FMA7097.definition: A cardiac atrium that is in the left side of the heart. It receives oxygenated blood from the pulmonary veins, In mammals this is pumped into the left ventricle, via the Mitral valve.

FMA7098.name: heart right ventricle
FMA7098.definition: A cardiac ventricle that is in the right side of the heart.

FMA7101.name: heart left ventricle
FMA7101.definition: A cardiac ventricle that is in the left side of the heart.

FMA71012.name: cutaneous appendage
FMA71012.definition: Anatomical projection that protrudes from the skin. Examples: hair, nail, feather, claw, hoof, horn, wattle, spur, beak, antler, bristle and some scales.

FMA71114.name: brachium of inferior colliculus
FMA71114.definition: The Brachium of inferior colliculus (or inferior brachium) carries auditory afferent fibers from the inferior colliculus of the mesencephalon to the medial geniculate nucleus. [WP,unvetted].

FMA71132.name: alimentary part of gastrointestinal system
FMA71132.definition: The part of the digestive system that excludes the hepatobiliary system.

FMA71193.name: thymus lobe
FMA71193.definition: Either of the two lateral lobes that constitute the thymus.

FMA71194.name: right thymus lobe
FMA71194.definition: A thymus lobe that is in the right side of a thymus.

FMA71195.name: left thymus lobe
FMA71195.definition: A thymus lobe that is in the left side of a thymus.

FMA71210.name: lateral thoracic vein
FMA71210.definition: The lateral thoracic vein is a tributary of the axillary vein. It runs with the lateral thoracic artery and drains the serratus ventralis muscle and the Pectoralis major muscle. Normally, the thoracoepigastric vein exists between this vein and superficial epigastric vein (a tributary of femoral vein), to act as a shunt for blood if the portal system (through the liver) develops hypertension or a blockage.

FMA71213.name: thoracodorsal vein
FMA71213.definition: Companion vein of the thoracodorsal artery, draining the apical part of the latissimus dorsi and merging with the circumflex scapular vein to form a subscapular vein.

FMA71221.name: postcranial axial skeleton
FMA71221.definition: The postcranial subdivision of skeleton structural components forming the long axis of the vertebrate body; in Danio, consisting of the notochord, vertebrae, ribs, supraneurals, intermuscular bones, and unpaired median fins; in human consists of the bones of the vertebral column, the thoracic cage and the pelvis[ZFA+FMA].

FMA7131.name: esophagus
FMA7131.definition: Tube that connects the pharynx to the stomach. In mammals, the oesophagus connects the buccal cavity with the stomach. The stratified squamous non-keratinised epithelium lining the buccal cavity is continued through the pharynx down into the oesophagus. The lowest part of the oesophagus (ca. 2 cm) is lined with gastric mucosa and covered by peritoneum.

FMA7145.name: membrane organ
FMA7145.definition: Nonparenchymatous organ that primarily consists of dense connective tissue organized into a sheet which interconnects two or more organs, separates two or more body spaces from one another, or surrounds an organ or body part. Examples: interosseous membrane of forearm, obturator membrane, tympanic membrane, fibrous pericardium, fascia lata, dura mater. [FMA].

FMA7146.name: gland
FMA7146.definition: An organ that functions as a secretory or excretory organ.

FMA7148.name: stomach
FMA7148.definition: An expanded region of the vertebrate alimentary tract that serves as a food storage compartment and digestive organ. A stomach is lined, in whole or in part by a glandular epithelium.

FMA7152.name: digestive system
FMA7152.definition: Anatomical system that has as its parts the organs devoted to the ingestion, digestion, and assimilation of food and the discharge of residual wastes.

FMA7154.name: head
FMA7154.definition: The head is the anterior-most division of the body [GO].

FMA7155.name: neck
FMA7155.definition: An organism subdivision that extends from the head to the pectoral girdle, encompassing the cervical vertebral column.

FMA7157.name: nervous system
FMA7157.definition: The nervous system is an organ system containing predominantly neuron and glial cells. In bilaterally symmetrical organism, it is arranged in a network of tree-like structures connected to a central body. The main functions of the nervous system are to regulate and control body functions, and to receive sensory input, process this information, and generate behavior [CUMBO].

FMA7158.name: respiratory system
FMA7158.definition: Functional system which consists of structures involved in respiration.

FMA7159.name: renal system
FMA7159.definition: The renal system in an anatomical system that maintains fluid balance and contributes to electrolyte balance, acid/base balance, and disposal of nitrogenous waste products.

FMA7160.name: reproductive system
FMA7160.definition: Anatomical system that has as its parts the organs concerned with reproduction.

FMA7161.name: cardiovascular system
FMA7161.definition: Anatomical system that has as its parts the heart and blood vessels.

FMA7163.name: skin of body
FMA7163.definition: The organ covering the body that consists of the dermis and epidermis.

FMA7165.name: right cardiac chamber
FMA7165.definition: Any chamber of the right side of the heart.

FMA7166.name: left cardiac chamber
FMA7166.definition: Any chamber of the left side of the heart.

FMA7181.name: trunk
FMA7181.definition: Organism subdivision which is the part of the body posterior to the cervical region (or head, when cervical region not present) and anterior to the caudal region. Includes the sacrum when present.

FMA7184.name: pelvic complex
FMA7184.definition: Appendage girdle complex that when present, encompasses the pelvic appendicular skeleton and the pelvic girdle.
synonyms: pelvic girdle plus pelvic limb or fin
pelvic girdle plus posterior limb or fin

FMA7185.name: right forelimb
FMA7185.definition: A forelimb that is on the right side of a pectoral complex.

FMA7186.name: left forelimb
FMA7186.definition: A forelimb that is on the left side of a pectoral complex.

FMA7187.name: right hindlimb
FMA7187.definition: A hindlimb that is on the right side of a pelvic complex.

FMA7188.name: left hindlimb
FMA7188.definition: A hindlimb that is on the left side of a pelvic complex.

FMA71891.name: hepatic duct
FMA71891.definition: Any portion of the ducts that carry bile from the liver to the common bile duct. This may include both intrahapetic components (parts of left and right hepatic ducts) and extrahapetic components (common hepatic duct, plus hilar portion).

FMA7196.name: spleen
FMA7196.definition: The organ that functions to filter blood and to store red corpuscles and platelets.

FMA7197.name: liver
FMA7197.definition: An exocrine gland which secretes bile and functions in metabolism of protein and carbohydrate and fat, synthesizes substances involved in the clotting of the blood, synthesizes vitamin A, detoxifies poisonous substances, stores glycogen, and breaks down worn-out erythrocytes[GO].

FMA7198.name: pancreas
FMA7198.definition: An endoderm derived structure that produces precursors of digestive enzymes and blood glucose regulating hormones[GO].

FMA7200.name: small intestine
FMA7200.definition: Subdivision of digestive tract that connects the stomach to the large intestine and is where much of the digestion and absorption of food takes place (with the exception of ruminants). The mammalian small intestine is long and coiled and can be differentiated histologically into: duodenum, jejunem, ileum[WP,cjm,Kardong].

FMA7201.name: large intestine
FMA7201.definition: A subdivision of the digestive tract that connects the small intestine to the cloaca or anus. Lacks or has few villi[Kardong].

FMA7202.name: gallbladder
FMA7202.definition: An organ that aids digestion and stores bile produced by the liver[WP].

FMA7203.name: adult mammalian kidney
FMA7203.definition: A kidney at the most advanced stage of development in a mammal.

FMA7206.name: duodenum
FMA7206.definition: The first part of the small intestine. At the junction of the stomach and the duodenum the alimentary canal is inflected. The duodenum first goes anteriorly for a short distance, turns dorsally, and eventually caudally, thus it is a U-shaped structure with two horizontal sections (a ventral and a dorsal one).

FMA7207.name: jejunum
FMA7207.definition: The portion of the small intestine that extends from the duodenum to the ileum.

FMA7208.name: ileum
FMA7208.definition: The portion of the small intestine that extends from the jejunum to the colon.

FMA7210.name: testis
FMA7210.definition: A gonad of a male animal. A gonad produces and releases sperm.

FMA7216.name: outflow part of right ventricle
FMA7216.definition: Anteriosuperior, smooth-walled portion of the cavity of the right ventricle, beginning at the supraventricular crest and terminating in the pulmonary trunk.

FMA72308.name: stylohyoid ligament
FMA72308.definition: The fibrous cord that connects the tip of the styloid process of the temporal bone to the lesser horn of the hyoid bone.

FMA7232.name: cusp of cardiac valve
FMA7232.definition: The part of the heart valves that serves to seal the heart valves when closed. There are three cusps for each valve except for the mitral valve, which has only two (hence its alternate name, 'bicuspid valve'). 'Nodules' are located at the tip of the valve, to form a tighter seal[WP].

FMA7234.name: tricuspid valve
FMA7234.definition: An atrioventricular valve that is part of the outflow part of the right atrium.

FMA7235.name: mitral valve
FMA7235.definition: An atrioventricular valve that is part of the outflow part of the left atrium.

FMA7236.name: aortic valve
FMA7236.definition: Cardiac valve which has as its parts the anterior, right posterior and left posterior cusps, attached to the fibrous ring of aortic valve.[FMA].

FMA7237.name: tricuspid valve leaflet
FMA7237.definition: A valve leaflet that is part of a tricuspid valve.

FMA7240.name: tricuspid valve cusp
FMA7240.definition: The three fibrous triangular components and associated flaps of the tricuspid valve.
synonyms: septal cusp of right atrioventricular valve
septal leaflet of right-sided tricuspid valve

FMA7241.name: mitral valve leaflet
FMA7241.definition: A valve leafleft that is part of a mitral valve.

FMA72417.name: brachium of superior colliculus
FMA72417.definition: Bundle of fibers that passes over the medial geniculate nucleus (in humans) to reach the superior colliculus. Contains afferents from the retina.

FMA7242.name: anterior leaflet of mitral valve
FMA7242.definition: Leaflet of mitral valve which is attached to the anterior head of the posterior papillary muscle of left ventricle through the chorda tendinea of the left ventricle.
synonyms: aortic leaflet of the left-sided mitral valve

FMA7243.name: posterior leaflet of mitral valve
FMA7243.definition: Leaflet of mitral valve which is attached to the posterior head of the lateral papillary muscle of left ventricle through the chorda tendinea of the left ventricle.

FMA7246.name: pulmonary valve
FMA7246.definition: The semilunar valve of the heart that lies between the right ventricle and the pulmonary artery.

FMA7248.name: pulmonary valve cusp
FMA7248.definition: The three fibrous triangular components and associated flap of the pulmonary valve.

FMA7251.name: aortic valve cusp
FMA7251.definition: The three fibrous triangular components and associated flap of the aortic valve.

FMA72828.name: right putamen
FMA72828.definition: A putamen that is part of a right cerebral hemisphere.

FMA72829.name: left putamen
FMA72829.definition: A putamen that is part of a left cerebral hemisphere.

FMA72969.name: right frontal lobe
FMA72969.definition: A frontal cortex that is part of a right cerebral hemisphere.

FMA72970.name: left frontal lobe
FMA72970.definition: A frontal cortex that is part of a left cerebral hemisphere.

FMA72971.name: right temporal lobe
FMA72971.definition: A temporal lobe that is part of a right cerebral hemisphere.

FMA72972.name: left temporal lobe
FMA72972.definition: A temporal lobe that is part of a left cerebral hemisphere.

FMA72973.name: right parietal lobe
FMA72973.definition: Parietal lobe of the right hemisphere of the brain.

FMA72974.name: left parietal lobe
FMA72974.definition: Parietal lobe of the left hemisphere of the brain.

FMA72975.name: right occipital lobe
FMA72975.definition: An occipital lobe that is part of a right cerebral hemisphere.

FMA72976.name: left occipital lobe
FMA72976.definition: An occipital lobe that is part of a left cerebral hemisphere.

FMA72979.name: integumental system
FMA72979.definition: Connected anatomical system that forms a barrier between an animal and its environment. In vertebrates, the integumental system consists of the epidermis, dermis plus associated glands and adnexa such as hair and scales. In invertebrates, the integumental system may include cuticle.

FMA72980.name: right limbic lobe
FMA72980.definition: A limbic lobe that is part of a right cerebral hemisphere.

FMA72981.name: left limbic lobe
FMA72981.definition: A limbic lobe that is part of a left cerebral hemisphere.

FMA7309.name: right lung
FMA7309.definition: Lung which consists of the right upper lobe, middle lobe and right lower lobe.[FMA].

FMA7310.name: left lung
FMA7310.definition: Lung which consists of the left upper lobe and left lower lobe.[FMA].

FMA7333.name: upper lobe of right lung
FMA7333.definition: The lobe of the right lung that is closest to the head.

FMA7337.name: lower lobe of right lung
FMA7337.definition: The lobe of the right lung that is furtherst from the head.

FMA7370.name: upper lobe of left lung
FMA7370.definition: The lobe of the left lung that is closest to the head.

FMA7371.name: lower lobe of left lung
FMA7371.definition: A lower lobe of lung that is part of a left lung.

FMA7383.name: middle lobe of right lung
FMA7383.definition: In the human, the right lung is divided into three lobes (as opposed to two lobes on the left), superior, middle, and inferior, by two interlobular fissures: [WP,unvetted].

FMA7393.name: tracheobronchial tree
FMA7393.definition: The structure from the trachea, bronchi, and bronchioles that forms the airways that supply air to the lungs. The lining of the tracheobronchial tree consists of ciliated columnar epithelial cells.

FMA7394.name: trachea
FMA7394.definition: The trachea is the portion of the airway that attaches to the bronchi as it branches [GO:dph].

FMA7395.name: right main bronchus
FMA7395.definition: The main bronchus on the right side.

FMA7396.name: left main bronchus
FMA7396.definition: The main bronchus on the left side.

FMA7405.name: main bronchus
FMA7405.definition: One of two branches of the trachea.

FMA7409.name: bronchus
FMA7409.definition: The upper conducting airways of the lung; these airways arise from the terminus of the trachea.

FMA7474.name: long bone
FMA7474.definition: A long bone is a bone that has a shaft and 2 ends and is longer than it is wide. Long bones have a thick outside layer of compact bone and an inner medullary cavity containing bone marrow. The ends of a long bone contain spongy bone and an epiphyseal plate or line depending on the stage of development.

FMA7475.name: short bone
FMA7475.definition: Short bones are designated as those bones that are as wide as they are long. Their primary function is to provide support and stability with little to no movement. They are one of five types of bones: long, short, flat, irregular and sesamoid. Examples of these bones include the tarsals in the foot and the carpals in the hand.

FMA7476.name: flat bone
FMA7476.definition: A bone that is shaped as a broad flat plate and composed of two thin layers of compact tissue enclosing between them a variable quantity of cancellous tissue, which is the location of red bone marrow.

FMA7477.name: irregular bone
FMA7477.definition: The irregular bones are bones which, from their peculiar form, cannot be grouped as long bone, short bone, flat bone or sesamoid bone. Irregular bones serve various purposes in the body, such as protection of nervous tissue, affording multiple anchor points for skeletal muscle attachment (as with the sacrum), and maintaining pharynx and trachea support, and tongue attachment (such as the hyoid bone).

FMA7478.name: pneumatized bone
FMA7478.definition: A bone that is hollow or contains many air cells, such as the mastoid process of the temporal bone[TMD].

FMA7480.name: thoracic rib cage
FMA7480.definition: Subdivision of skeletal system that consists of all ribs in an organism connected to the sternum and the vertebrae. Some vertebrates have abdominal ribs (gastrialia), not connected to the vertebrate - these are not considered part of the rib case.

FMA7482.name: musculoskeletal system
FMA7482.definition: Anatomical system that consists of the muscular and skeletal systems.

FMA7483.name: axial skeletal system
FMA7483.definition: Subdivision of the skeletal system which consists of the axial skeleton plus associated joints.

FMA7485.name: sternum
FMA7485.definition: A midventral endochondral skeletal element which represents the origin site of the pectoral muscles[PHENOSCAPE:ad].

FMA7486.name: manubrium of sternum
FMA7486.definition: The cranial most segment of the sternum. Located ventrally with a quadrangular shape, wider superiorly and narrower inferiorly, it articulates with the clavicles and the first two ribs[MP,WP].

FMA7487.name: body of sternum
FMA7487.definition: The middle and longest portion of the sternum, lying between the manubrium superiorly and the xiphoid process inferiorly; it considerably lengthier, narrower, and thinner than the manubrium, attains its greatest breadth close to the lower end.

FMA74877.name: mammillary body
FMA74877.definition: One of two hemispherical bulges on the base of the posterior hypothalamus (Butler and Hodos, Comparative Vertebrate Neuroanatomy, 2nd ed., 2005, pg 455).

FMA7488.name: xiphoid process
FMA7488.definition: A cartilaginous extension to the distal part of the sternum.

FMA75007.name: lumen of central nervous system
FMA75007.definition: The cavity that is enclosed by the central nervous system. In vertebrates this is the cavity that includes as parts ventricular cavities and the central canal of the spinal cord that develops from the lumen of the neura tube.
synonyms: cavity of ventricular system of neuraxis

FMA75351.name: interventricular foramen of CNS
FMA75351.definition: The paired channels that connect the lateral and third ventricles and allows cerebrospinal fluid produced in the lateral ventricles to flow into the third ventricles.

FMA7574.name: rib
FMA7574.definition: An intersegmental rod-shaped bone that forms in the peritoneal membrane and attach to the vertebral parapophyses.

FMA7591.name: costal cartilage
FMA7591.definition: The nonvascular, resilient, flexible hyaline connective tissue that connects the end of a true rib to the sternum or the end of a false rib with the with the lower border of the costal cartilage above it.

FMA7592.name: true rib
FMA7592.definition: A rib that is ventrally connected to the sternum.

FMA7594.name: false rib
FMA7594.definition: A rib that is not directly ventrally connected to the sternum.

FMA7595.name: floating rib
FMA7595.definition: A rib that is not connected to sternum or sternal cartilage.

FMA7597.name: rib 1
FMA7597.definition: The first rib of the rib cage.

FMA7620.name: rib 2
FMA7620.definition: The second rib of the rib cage.

FMA7638.name: rib 3
FMA7638.definition: The third rib counting from the top of the rib cage down. Note that members of this class are not necessarily homologous[ncit,modified].

FMA7647.name: spinal cord
FMA7647.definition: Part of the central nervous system located in the vertebral canal continuous with and caudal to the brain; demarcated from brain by plane of foramen magnum. It is composed of an inner core of gray matter in which nerve cells predominate, and an outer layer of white matter in which myelinated nerve fibers predominate, and surrounds the central canal. (CUMBO).

FMA76998.name: dorsal intercostal artery
FMA76998.definition: The highest intercostal artery (supreme intercostal artery, superior intercostal artery) is an artery in the human body that usually gives rise to the first and second posterior intercostal arteries, which supply blood to their corresponding intercostal space. It usually arises from the costocervical trunk, which is a branch of the subclavian artery.

FMA77155.name: popliteal artery
FMA77155.definition: The continuation of the femoral artery coursing through the popliteal fossa; it divides into the anterior and posterior tibial arteries.

FMA77168.name: median sacral vein
FMA77168.definition: The median sacral vein (or middle sacral veins) accompany the corresponding artery along the front of the sacrum, and join to form a single vein, which ends in the left common iliac vein; sometimes in the angle of junction of the two iliac veins.

FMA77177.name: iliocostalis muscle
FMA77177.definition: The iliocostalis is the muscle immediately lateral to the longissimus that is the nearest to the furrow that separates the epaxial muscles from the hypaxial. It lies very deep to the fleshy portion of the serratus ventralis (serratus anterior). [WP,unvetted].

FMA77178.name: longissimus muscle
FMA77178.definition: The longissimus is the muscle lateral to the semispinalis. It is the longest subdivision of the sacrospinalis that extends forward into the transverse processes of the posterior cervical vertebrae. [WP,unvetted].

FMA77179.name: spinalis muscle
FMA77179.definition: The spinalis is the portion of the erector spinae, a bundle of muscles and tendons, located nearest to the spine. It is divided into three parts. [WP,unvetted].

FMA77180.name: splenius
FMA77180.definition: A superficial postvertebral muscle innervated by the posterior ramus of the cervical spinal nerve with origins in the upper thoracic and lower cervical spinous processes whose actions are to extend and ipsilaterally rotate the head and neck. Examples: splenius capitis, splenius cervicis.

FMA7749.name: rib 4
FMA7749.definition: The fourth rib counting from the top of the rib cage down. Note that members of this class are not necessarily homologous[ncit,modified].

FMA7776.name: rib 5
FMA7776.definition: The fifth rib counting from the top of the rib cage down. Note that members of this class are not necessarily homologous[ncit,modified].

FMA78121.name: superior phrenic vein
FMA78121.definition: The superior phrenic vein, i.e. , the vein accompanying the pericardiacophrenic artery, usually opens into the internal mammary vein.

FMA7830.name: rib 7
FMA7830.definition: The seventh rib counting from the top of the rib cage down. Note that members of this class are not necessarily homologous[ncit,modified].

FMA78447.name: brain ventricle
FMA78447.definition: One of the system of communicating cavities in the brain that are continuous with the central canal of the spinal cord, that like it are derived from the medullary canal of the embryo, that are lined with an epithelial ependyma, and that contain a serous fluid.
synonyms: region of ventricular system of brain

FMA78448.name: telencephalic ventricle
FMA78448.definition: A brain ventricle that is part of a telencephalon. In mammals and species with an evaginated telencephalon, this is one of a pair of lateral structures, one in each hemisphere.

FMA78449.name: right lateral ventricle
FMA78449.definition: A telencephalic ventricle that is in_the_right_side_of a telencephalon.

FMA78450.name: left lateral ventricle
FMA78450.definition: A telencephalic ventricle that is in_the_left_side_of a telencephalon.

FMA78454.name: third ventricle
FMA78454.definition: Part of the ventricular system of the brain, forming a single large cavity in the midline of the diencephalon; it is continuous with the lateral ventricles through the interventricular foramen and the fourth ventricle through the cerebral aqueduct. (Maryann Martone).

FMA78467.name: midbrain cerebral aqueduct
FMA78467.definition: Part of ventricular system of brain consisting of a narrow channel in the midbrain connecting the third and fourth ventricles. (Maryann Martone).

FMA78469.name: fourth ventricle
FMA78469.definition: Part of the ventricular system of the brain, forming a single large irregularly shaped cavity located on the midline of the rhombencephalon, between the medulla, pons and the isthmus ventrally and the cerebellum dorsally. It is continuous with the cerebral aqueduct anteriorally and the central canal of the spinal cord posteriorly. It communicates with the subarachnoid space through its lateral and median apertures.

FMA78497.name: central canal of spinal cord
FMA78497.definition: Spinal cord structure that is part of the ventricular system and is filled with cerebral-spinal fluid and runs the length of the spinal cord.

FMA79876.name: brainstem
FMA79876.definition: Stalk-like part of the brain that includes amongst its parts the medulla oblongata of the hindbrain and the tegmentum of the midbrain[ZFA,MP,generalized].

FMA8120.name: rib 8
FMA8120.definition: The eighth rib counting from the top of the rib cage down. Note that members of this class are not necessarily homologous[ncit,modified].

FMA8147.name: rib 6
FMA8147.definition: The sixth rib counting from the top of the rib cage down. Note that members of this class are not necessarily homologous[ncit,modified].

FMA82472.name: organ part
FMA82472.definition: A multicellular structure that is a part of an organ.

FMA82485.name: organ component layer
FMA82485.definition: A part of a wall of an organ that forms a layer.

FMA83115.name: multi cell part structure
FMA83115.definition: A structure consisting mainly of cell components, rather than complete cells.

FMA83143.name: central nervous system cell part cluster
FMA83143.definition: A multi cell part structure that is part of a central nervous system.

FMA8337.name: rib 9
FMA8337.definition: The ninth rib counting from the top of the rib cage down. Note that members of this class are not necessarily homologous[ncit,modified].

FMA83686.name: neural nucleus
FMA83686.definition: A spatially aggregated collection of nerve cell bodies in the CNS, consisting of one or more subpopulations that share cell type, chemical phenotype, and connections, and including nearby cells that share the same cell type, chemical phenotype, and connections. (CUMBO).

FMA83840.name: nucleus of brain
FMA83840.definition: A neural nucleus that is part of the brain.

FMA83865.name: fornix of brain
FMA83865.definition: A C-shaped bundle of fibres (axons) in the brain, and carries signals from the hippocampus to the mammillary bodies and septal nuclei. It is typically divided into the columns (crus), body, commissure and the pre-commissural and post-commissural fornix (MM).

FMA83874.name: gyrus
FMA83874.definition: A ridge on the cerebral cortex. It is generally surrounded by one or more sulci .

FMA83902.name: midbrain tectum
FMA83902.definition: Dorsal part of the midbrain, consisting of the superior and inferior colliculi and the pretectal nuclei (MM).

FMA83906.name: nervous system commissure
FMA83906.definition: Axon tract that crosses the midline of the central nervous system[NIF, modified]. In the context of Drosophila refers to a broad band of axons connecting equivalent neuropils each side of the brain[FBbt].

FMA83929.name: white matter
FMA83929.definition: Neural tissue consisting of myelinated axons connecting grey matter areas of the central nervous system.

FMA83930.name: white matter of telencephalon
FMA83930.definition: A partion of white matter that is part of a telencephalon. This can be further subdivided in some species, for example, into hemisphere white matter and the corpus callosum.
synonyms: predominantly white regional part of telencephalon

FMA83966.name: tentorium cerebelli
FMA83966.definition: The tentorium cerebelli or cerebellar tentorium is an extension of the dura mater that separates the cerebellum from the inferior portion of the occipital lobes.

FMA84059.name: nuclear complex of neuraxis
FMA84059.definition: Gray matter of the central nervous system which is a collection of clustered nuclei.

FMA84081.name: circumventricular organ
FMA84081.definition: Any of any of the secretory or sensory organs located in the brain region around or in relation to the ventricular system that are characterized by extensive vasculature and a lack of a normal blood brain barrier (BBB) and allow for the linkage between the central nervous system and peripheral blood flow.

FMA8418.name: rib 10
FMA8418.definition: The tenth rib has only a single articular facet on its head. [WP,unvetted].

FMA8499.name: rib 11
FMA8499.definition: The eleventh rib has a single articular facet on the head, which is of rather large size. It has no necks or tubercles, and is pointed at its anterior ends. The eleventh has a slight angle and a shallow costal groove. [WP,unvetted].

FMA8515.name: rib 12
FMA8515.definition: In humans: The twelfth rib has a single articular facet on the head, which is of rather large size. It has no necks or tubercles, and is pointed at its anterior ends. The twelfth has angle nor costal groove; it is much shorter than the eleventh rib, and its head is inclined slightly downward. Sometimes the twelfth rib is even shorter than the first rib. [WP,unvetted].

FMA8612.name: pulmonary trunk
FMA8612.definition: An arterial trunk which is continuous with the heart and branches into the pulmonary arteries.

FMA86140.name: organ subunit
FMA86140.definition: A part of an organ that constitutes a distinct modular sub-unit. In some cases, the organ may also contain other sub-units of identical or similar types, in other cases this may be a distinct entity.

FMA86188.name: venous blood vessel
FMA86188.definition: A blood vessel that carries blood from the capillaries toward the heart.

FMA86464.name: corpus callosum
FMA86464.definition: White matter structure containing massive numbers of commissural fibers connecting cortical areas in the two cerebral hemispheres. It is subdivided into a genu, a rostrum, a body, and a splenium. (MM).

FMA86917.name: abdomen musculature
FMA86917.definition: Set of all muscles in abdomen.

FMA87217.name: descending thoracic aorta
FMA87217.definition: The part of the aorta that extends from the arch of the aorta to the diaphragm, and from which arises numerous branches that supply oxygenated blood to the chest cage and the organs within the chest.

FMA9139.name: thoracic vertebra
FMA9139.definition: A thoracic vertebra endochondral element that is composed primarily of a bone tissue.

FMA9140.name: thoracic region of vertebral column
FMA9140.definition: That part of the spine comprising the thoracic vertebrae.

FMA9165.name: thoracic vertebra 1
FMA9165.definition: The first thoracic vertebra counting from the top down. Note that members of this class are not necessarily homologous[ncit,modified].

FMA9187.name: thoracic vertebra 2
FMA9187.definition: The second thoracic vertebra counting from the top down. Note that members of this class are not necessarily homologous[ncit,modified].

FMA9209.name: thoracic vertebra 3
FMA9209.definition: The third thoracic vertebra counting from the top down. Note that members of this class are not necessarily homologous[ncit,modified].

FMA9248.name: thoracic vertebra 4
FMA9248.definition: The fourth thoracic vertebra counting from the top down. Note that members of this class are not necessarily homologous[ncit,modified].

FMA9291.name: cavity of right ventricle
FMA9291.definition: Luminal space of the right ventricle of the heart.

FMA9311.name: subsegmental pulmonary artery
FMA9311.definition: An artery that is a branch of the segmental pulmonary artery and supplies deoxyge blood to a smaller subsegment of the lung.

FMA9338.name: anatomical conduit space
FMA9338.definition: An anatomical space which is the lumen of some anatomical conduit and connects two or more spaces together[FMA,modified].

FMA9411.name: segmental pulmonary vein
FMA9411.definition: A vein that is tributary of the main pulmonary veins and drains oxygenated blood from a segment of the lung.

FMA9413.name: subsegmental pulmonary vein
FMA9413.definition: A vein that is tributary of the segmental pulmonary veins and drains oxygenated blood from a subsegment of the lung.

FMA9465.name: cavity of left atrium
FMA9465.definition: Luminal space of the left atrium of the heart.

FMA9466.name: cavity of left ventricle
FMA9466.definition: Luminal space of the left ventricle of the heart.

FMA9473.name: outflow part of left ventricle
FMA9473.definition: Anterosuperior fibrous portion of the left ventricle that connects to the ascending aorta.

FMA9496.name: cardiac skeleton
FMA9496.definition: Dense connective tissue that separates the atria from the ventricles and provides physical support for the heart.

FMA9498.name: mitral valve anulus
FMA9498.definition: The fibrous ring of the mitral valve that attaches the cusps of mitral valve to the heart, and which consists of portions of the fibrous scallops of the anterior and posterior cusps.

FMA9533.name: wall of right ventricle
FMA9533.definition: Wall of ventricle which is continuous with the wall of pulmonary trunk.

FMA9535.name: right ventricle myocardium
FMA9535.definition: A myocardium that is part of a right ventricle of a heart.

FMA9550.name: outflow part of right atrium
FMA9550.definition: Outflow part of atrium which consists of wall and cavity of the outflow part of right atrium and the tricuspid valve.[FMA].

FMA9551.name: outflow part of left atrium
FMA9551.definition: An outflow tract of atrium that is part of a left atrium.

FMA9553.name: anterior wall of right ventricle
FMA9553.definition: Region of wall of right ventricle which is continuous with the lateral and septal walls of right ventricle.

FMA9556.name: wall of left ventricle
FMA9556.definition: Wall of ventricle which is continuous with the wall of aorta.

FMA9558.name: left ventricle myocardium
FMA9558.definition: A myocardium that is part of a left ventricle of a heart.

FMA9576.name: chest
FMA9576.definition: Subdivision of trunk proper, which is demarcated from the neck by the plane of the superior thoracic aperture and from the abdomen internally by the inferior surface of the diaphragm and externally by the costal margin and associated with the thoracic vertebral column and ribcage and from the back of the thorax by the external surface of the posterolateral part of the rib cage, the anterior surface of the thoracic vertebral column and the posterior axillary lines; together with the abdomen and the perineum, it constitutes the trunk proper[FMA].

FMA9577.name: abdomen
FMA9577.definition: The subdivision of the vertebrate body between the thorax and pelvis. The ventral part of the abdomen contains the abdominal cavity and visceral organs. The dorsal part includes the abdominal section of the vertebral column.

FMA9578.name: pelvic region of trunk
FMA9578.definition: The lower segment of the trunk, inferioposterior to the abdomen proper, in the transition area between the trunk and the lower limbs.

FMA9579.name: perineum
FMA9579.definition: Subdivision of trunk proper, which is demarcated from the pelvis by the inferior surface of the pelvic diaphragm and from the lower limbs by the perineofemoral lines; together with the thorax, abdomen, and pelvis, it constitutes the trunk[FMA].

FMA9584.name: peritoneum
FMA9584.definition: A serous membrane that lines the peritoneal cavity[VHOG,modified].

FMA9597.name: saliva-secreting gland
FMA9597.definition: Saliva-secreting exocrine glands of the oral cavity[GO].

FMA9600.name: prostate gland
FMA9600.definition: The prostate gland is a partly muscular, partly glandular body that is situated near the base of the mammalian male urethra and secretes an alkaline viscid fluid which is a major constituent of the ejaculatory fluid.

FMA9604.name: adrenal gland
FMA9604.definition: Either of a pair of complex endocrine organs near the anterior medial border of the kidney consisting of a mesodermal cortex that produces glucocorticoid, mineralocorticoid, and androgenic hormones and an ectodermal medulla that produces epinephrine and norepinephrine[BTO].

FMA9607.name: thymus
FMA9607.definition: Anatomical structure of largely lymphoid tissue that functions in cell-mediated immunity by being the site where T cells develop.

FMA9611.name: femur
FMA9611.definition: Endochondral longbone connecting the pelvic girdle with posterior zeugopodium skeleton.[VSAO, modified].

FMA9612.name: metacarpal bone
FMA9612.definition: A bone that is part of the metacarpal skeleton.

FMA9613.name: tetrapod parietal bone
FMA9613.definition: In humans: bone forming side and roof of cranium. Each bone is irregularly quadrilateral in form, and has two surfaces, four borders, and four angles.

FMA9615.name: cricoid cartilage
FMA9615.definition: A cartilaginous ring that provides support for the arytenoid cartilages and forms the caudal part of the larynx.

FMA9616.name: cranial muscle
FMA9616.definition: Any skeletal muscle that is part of the head region.

FMA9617.name: muscle of neck
FMA9617.definition: Any muscle that is part of the cervical (neck) region.

FMA9619.name: chest muscle
synonyms: anterolateral part of thorax muscle organ
muscle organ of anterior thoracic region

FMA9620.name: muscle of abdomen
FMA9620.definition: Muscle (organ) which is a part of the abdomen. Examples: external oblique, rectus abdominis.

FMA9621.name: pectoral complex muscle
FMA9621.definition: A muscle of a pectoral girdle, pectoral fin or anterior limb.
synonyms: pectoral girdle and fore limb muscles

FMA9622.name: pelvic complex muscle
FMA9622.definition: Muscles of the pelvic girdle, hindlimb or pelvic fin.
synonyms: pelvic girdle and hind limb muscles

FMA9625.name: stylohyoid muscle
FMA9625.definition: The stylohyoid is a pharyngeal arch II muscle that participates in oral/pharygeal behaviors and is innervated by the stylohoid branch of the facial nerve and attaches to the stylohyal and the non-stylohyal part of the hyoid apparatus.

FMA9629.name: supraspinatus muscle
FMA9629.definition: The supraspinatus is a relatively small muscle of the upper limb that takes its name from its origin from the supraspinous fossa superior to the spine of the scapula. It is one of the four rotator cuff muscles and also abducts the arm at the shoulder. The spine of the scapula separates the supraspinatus muscle from the infraspinatus muscle, which originates below the spine. [WP,unvetted].

FMA9637.name: tissue
FMA9637.definition: Multicellular anatomical structure that consists of many cells of one or a few types, arranged in an extracellular matrix such that their long-range organisation is at least partly a repetition of their short-range organisation.

FMA9640.name: connective tissue
FMA9640.definition: Tissue with cells that deposit non-polarized extracellular matrix including connective tissue fibers and ground substance.

FMA9657.name: anatomical line
FMA9657.definition: Non-material anatomical entity of one dimension, which forms a boundary of an anatomical surface or is a modulation of an anatomical surface.

FMA9668.name: endocrine system
FMA9668.definition: Anatomical system that consists of the glands and parts of glands that produce endocrine secretions and help to integrate and control bodily metabolic activity.

FMA9703.name: nasolacrimal duct
FMA9703.definition: The paired channels leading from the lacrimal sacs to the inferior meatus of the nose, through which tears are conducted through the nasal cavity.

FMA9704.name: ureter
FMA9704.definition: Muscular duct that propels urine from the kidneys to the urinary bladder, or related organs.

FMA9706.name: bile duct
FMA9706.definition: Any of the ducts that form the biliary tree, carrying bile from the liver to the small intestine.

FMA9708.name: talus
FMA9708.definition: A proximal tarsal bone resulting from fusion of intermedium and fibulare.

FMA9710.name: vomer
FMA9710.definition: The triangular flat bone of the nasal septum.

FMA9711.name: maxilla
FMA9711.definition: The bone which normally forms the lateral upper jaw in osteichthyans, including tetrapods.

FMA9721.name: tendon
FMA9721.definition: Dense regular connective tissue that connects muscle to bone[VSAO].

FMA9756.name: external intercostal muscle
FMA9756.definition: An intercostal muscle that aids in quiet and forced inhalation via elevation of the ribs, and expanding the transverse dimensions of the thoracic cavity.

FMA9757.name: internal intercostal muscle
FMA9757.definition: An intercostal muscle that aids in forced expiration (quiet expiration is a passive process).

FMA9758.name: innermost intercostal muscle
FMA9758.definition: The Innermost intercostal muscle is a layer of intercostal muscle beneath the intercostal nerves and internal intercostal muscles. These are divided into transversus thoracis anteriorly, lateral muscle slips laterally and subcostalis posteriorly.

FMA9760.name: transversus thoracis
FMA9760.definition: The tranversus thoracis lies internal to the thoracic cage, anteriorly. It is a thin plane of muscular and tendinous fibers, situated upon the inner surface of the front wall of the chest. It is in the same layer as the subcostal muscles.

FMA9826.name: mediastinum
FMA9826.definition: The central part of the thoracic cavity enclosed by the left and right pleurae.

FMA9827.name: superior mediastinum
FMA9827.definition: The superior mediastinum is that portion of the interpleural space which lies between the manubrium sterni in front, and the upper thoracic vertebrae behind.

FMA9838.name: anterior mediastinum
FMA9838.definition: The anterior mediastinum exists only on the left side where the left pleura diverges from the mid-sternal line. It is narrow, above, but widens out a little below.

FMA9839.name: middle mediastinum
FMA9839.definition: The middle mediastinum is the broadest part of the interpleural space. It is made up of the pericardial sac and its contents.

FMA9840.name: posterior mediastinum
FMA9840.definition: The posterior mediastinum is an irregular triangular space running parallel with the vertebral column.

FMA9908.name: peritoneal sac
FMA9908.definition: A serous sac that is the aggregate of the peritoneum and the peritoneal cavity, located in the abdominal cavity.

FMA9914.name: vertebra
FMA9914.definition: The ossified form of a vertebral element, a skeletal element that forms around the notochord and is part of the vertebral column.

FMA9915.name: cervical vertebra
FMA9915.definition: A vertebra that is located in the cervical region of the vertebral column.

FMA9921.name: lumbar vertebra
FMA9921.definition: Large vertebra of the movable part of the vertebral column, characterized by the absence of the foramen transversarium within the transverse process, and by the absence of facets on the sides of the body.

FMA9922.name: thoracic vertebra 5
FMA9922.definition: The fifth thoracic vertebra counting from the top down. Note that members of this class are not necessarily homologous[ncit,modified].

FMA9945.name: thoracic vertebra 6
FMA9945.definition: The sixth thoracic vertebra counting from the top down. Note that members of this class are not necessarily homologous[ncit,modified].

FMA9968.name: thoracic vertebra 7
FMA9968.definition: The seventh thoracic vertebra counting from the top down. Note that members of this class are not necessarily homologous[ncit,modified].

FMA9991.name: thoracic vertebra 8
FMA9991.definition: The eighth thoracic vertebra counting from the top down. Note that members of this class are not necessarily homologous[ncit,modified].
